labs.title: Neurology & Neuro-Psych Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: NEUROLOGY / PSYCHIATRY CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY LEARNING WORKSPACE
labs.subtitle: Seizure phenotype → headache pathway → movement/cognition → mood/anxiety/psychosis → mechanism → generic → formulation → adult learning-dose → monitoring/source verification
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning pharmacology only. Neurologic and psychiatric medicines require diagnosis-specific selection, slow titration or tapering where appropriate, interaction review and close monitoring. Valproate, benzodiazepines, lithium, clozapine, anti-amyloid antibodies, antiseizure medicines in pregnancy, and emergency/status-seizure therapy have high-consequence safeguards. Do not infer a universal first-line drug from a class card. Verify current guideline/label, seizure syndrome, suicidality/mania risk, pregnancy potential, renal/hepatic function, ECG/QT, metabolic/EPS risk and controlled-drug rules before prescribing.

classification_notes.seizure_syndrome: Antiseizure medicine choice depends on focal vs generalized seizure type, epilepsy syndrome, age, comorbidity, reproductive potential and interaction profile. Narrow-spectrum sodium-channel agents can worsen some generalized epilepsies.
classification_notes.valproate_reproductive_safety: Valproate has major reproductive safety restrictions. Current national/regulatory rules and pregnancy-prevention requirements must be checked before use in people who could conceive; do not rely on a generic class summary.
classification_notes.migraine_acute_vs_preventive: Acute rescue and prevention are separate decisions. Medication-overuse headache, cardiovascular contraindications to vasoconstrictors, pregnancy, and attack frequency alter drug choice.
classification_notes.vestibular_suppression: Vestibular suppressants can be useful briefly for severe vertigo/nausea but prolonged use may delay central compensation; diagnose the cause and prioritize repositioning/rehabilitation when indicated.
classification_notes.parkinson_pharmacology: Levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT inhibitors and adjuncts differ in motor benefit, dyskinesia, impulse-control, hallucination, orthostasis and sleepiness risks; timing and advanced-device therapy are specialist-sensitive.
classification_notes.dementia_symptomatic_vs_disease_modifyin: Cholinesterase inhibitors/memantine are symptomatic therapies. Anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies are disease-modifying specialist therapies for selected biomarker-confirmed early Alzheimer disease with MRI/ARIA and anticoagulation-related considerations.
classification_notes.psych_diagnostic_gate: Before antidepressant escalation, assess bipolar-spectrum features, suicidality, substance use and medical causes. Antipsychotic choice requires metabolic, prolactin, QT/EPS and tardive-dyskinesia monitoring. Benzodiazepines are generally short-term/limited-use tools because of dependence, falls and withdrawal risk.
classification_notes.dose_boundary: Displayed doses are adult learning snapshots, not individualized prescriptions. Many drugs require syndrome-specific titration, therapeutic drug monitoring, renal/hepatic adjustment, slow withdrawal, or specialist initiation.

classes.name: Voltage-gated sodium-channel antiseizure medicines
classes.mechanism: Use-dependent sodium-channel inhibition stabilizes hyperexcitable neuronal membranes
classes.role_note: Major focal-seizure family; agent-specific interaction, cardiac, hyponatremia and rash profiles differ.

classes.name: SV2A ligands
classes.mechanism: Bind synaptic vesicle protein 2A and modulate neurotransmitter release
classes.role_note: Broadly used ASMs with relatively limited pharmacokinetic interactions; behavioral adverse effects matter.

classes.name: Broad-spectrum multi-mechanism ASMs
classes.mechanism: Multiple ion-channel and inhibitory/excitatory neurotransmitter effects
classes.role_note: Useful across seizure types but safety profiles differ greatly.

classes.name: T-type calcium-channel ASM
classes.mechanism: Reduces thalamic T-type calcium currents
classes.role_note: Classic pharmacology for absence seizures.

classes.name: Benzodiazepine antiseizure / rescue agents
classes.mechanism: Positive allosteric modulation of GABA-A increases inhibitory neurotransmission
classes.role_note: Rapid antiseizure effect; tolerance, sedation, respiratory depression and dependence limit chronic use.

classes.name: Barbiturate antiseizure medicines
classes.mechanism: Prolong GABA-A chloride-channel opening and depress CNS excitability
classes.role_note: Older effective ASMs with sedation, dependence and major interaction burden.

classes.name: α2δ calcium-channel ligands
classes.mechanism: Bind α2δ subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, reducing excitatory transmitter release
classes.role_note: Adjunct focal-seizure and neuropathic-pain pharmacology; renal clearance is important.

classes.name: Glutamatergic / AMPA antagonism ASMs
classes.mechanism: Reduce excitatory glutamate signaling at AMPA receptors
classes.role_note: Newer adjunctive antiseizure mechanism.

classes.name: Other newer / specialized ASMs
classes.mechanism: Diverse mechanisms including persistent sodium-current inhibition and endocannabinoid effects
classes.role_note: Specialist-focused options for refractory epilepsy.

classes.name: Triptans (5-HT1B/1D agonists)
classes.mechanism: Cranial vasoconstriction plus trigeminal neuropeptide inhibition
classes.role_note: Migraine-specific acute therapy; cardiovascular contraindications and medication-overuse risk must be checked.

classes.name: CGRP receptor antagonists (gepants) — acute
classes.mechanism: Block CGRP receptor signaling without triptan-like vasoconstriction
classes.role_note: Migraine-specific non-vasoconstrictor acute options; interaction/hepatic/renal limits vary.

classes.name: 5-HT1F agonist (ditan)
classes.mechanism: Selective 5-HT1F agonism reduces trigeminal signaling without 5-HT1B vasoconstriction
classes.role_note: Acute migraine option with prominent CNS impairment precautions.

classes.name: CGRP-pathway monoclonal antibodies — prevention
classes.mechanism: Neutralize CGRP ligand or block the CGRP receptor
classes.role_note: Migraine prevention with monthly/quarterly SC or IV dosing; selection depends on access and phenotype.

classes.name: Oral migraine preventives — multi-mechanism
classes.mechanism: Reduce cortical/trigeminovascular excitability via diverse targets
classes.role_note: Established oral prevention options; comorbidity often guides choice.

classes.name: Oral CGRP antagonists — prevention
classes.mechanism: CGRP receptor antagonism reduces migraine signaling
classes.role_note: Oral preventive CGRP pathway options.

classes.name: OnabotulinumtoxinA for chronic migraine
classes.mechanism: Blocks acetylcholine release at peripheral nerve terminals and modulates nociceptive signaling
classes.role_note: Procedure-based prevention for chronic migraine, not episodic migraine.

classes.name: Cluster-headache specific pharmacology
classes.mechanism: Acute trigeminal-autonomic attack termination and preventive modulation
classes.role_note: High-flow oxygen is non-drug first-line acute therapy; subcutaneous/nasal triptans and preventive verapamil are key pharmacologic concepts.

classes.name: Vestibular H1 antihistamines / anticholinergic suppressants
classes.mechanism: Reduce vestibular nucleus signaling through H1 and antimuscarinic effects
classes.role_note: Short-term symptomatic relief of acute vertigo/motion sickness; prolonged suppression can impair compensation.

classes.name: Dopamine-antagonist antiemetics for severe vertigo/nausea
classes.mechanism: D2 antagonism in chemoreceptor trigger zone with vestibular antiemetic effect
classes.role_note: Short-course antiemetic/vestibular suppression; EPS/QT risks matter.

classes.name: Histamine-modulating antivertigo therapy
classes.mechanism: H1 agonist/H3 antagonist activity may influence vestibular compensation and inner-ear microcirculation
classes.role_note: Used in Ménière-type vertigo in many countries; evidence/availability vary by jurisdiction.

classes.name: Levodopa + peripheral dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Levodopa crosses BBB and is converted to dopamine; carbidopa/benserazide reduces peripheral conversion
classes.role_note: Most effective symptomatic motor therapy; dose timing, protein interaction, wearing-off and dyskinesia matter.

classes.name: Dopamine agonists
classes.mechanism: Directly stimulate dopamine receptors
classes.role_note: Can delay/add to levodopa but carry impulse-control, hallucination, edema and sleep-attack risks.

classes.name: MAO-B inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Reduce dopamine breakdown by inhibiting monoamine oxidase-B
classes.role_note: Mild symptomatic/add-on therapy for wearing-off; interaction and serotonergic review required.

classes.name: COMT inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Inhibit peripheral (and for tolcapone central) levodopa metabolism, prolonging levodopa effect
classes.role_note: Adjuncts for levodopa wearing-off; no meaningful monotherapy role.

classes.name: Amantadine / NMDA-dopaminergic modulation
classes.mechanism: NMDA antagonism with dopaminergic effects
classes.role_note: Useful particularly for dyskinesia; renal clearance and neuropsychiatric effects matter.

classes.name: Central antimuscarinics for parkinsonian tremor
classes.mechanism: Block central muscarinic cholinergic activity
classes.role_note: Limited role, mainly tremor in younger selected patients; avoid in cognitive impairment/elderly when possible.

classes.name: Adenosine A2A antagonist
classes.mechanism: Blocks striatal adenosine A2A receptors to modulate indirect pathway signaling
classes.role_note: Add-on for OFF episodes in levodopa-treated Parkinson disease.

classes.name: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Increase synaptic acetylcholine by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase
classes.role_note: Symptomatic cognitive therapy in Alzheimer disease and selected dementias; bradycardia/GI burden matters.

classes.name: NMDA receptor antagonist for dementia
classes.mechanism: Moderate-affinity NMDA antagonism reduces pathologic glutamatergic excitotoxicity
classes.role_note: Symptomatic therapy for moderate–severe Alzheimer disease, alone or with AChEI.

classes.name: Anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies
classes.mechanism: Bind aggregated amyloid-β species to reduce cerebral amyloid burden
classes.role_note: Disease-modifying specialist therapy for selected biomarker-confirmed early Alzheimer disease; not routine symptomatic dementia treatment.

classes.name: Antiplatelet secondary-prevention pharmacology
classes.mechanism: Inhibit platelet activation/aggregation to reduce recurrent non-cardioembolic ischemic events
classes.role_note: Stroke prevention depends on stroke mechanism; short DAPT is only for selected acute minor stroke/TIA scenarios, not indefinite default therapy.

classes.name: High-intensity lipid lowering after atherosclerotic ischemic stroke
classes.mechanism: LDL reduction and plaque stabilization
classes.role_note: Secondary vascular prevention after atherosclerotic ischemic stroke; targets/intensification depend on vascular risk and tolerance.

classes.name: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs)
classes.mechanism: Block serotonin transporter and increase synaptic serotonin
classes.role_note: Common first-line antidepressant/anxiolytic family; individual agents differ in half-life, QT, interactions and withdrawal.

classes.name: Serotonin–norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs)
classes.mechanism: Block SERT and NET to increase serotonin and norepinephrine
classes.role_note: Depression/anxiety drugs with pain utility for some agents; BP and discontinuation effects matter.

classes.name: Atypical / multimodal antidepressants
classes.mechanism: Diverse monoaminergic mechanisms beyond classic SSRI/SNRI
classes.role_note: Useful when symptom profile or adverse-effect priorities favor a different mechanism.

classes.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
classes.mechanism: Inhibit serotonin/norepinephrine reuptake with varying anticholinergic/antihistamine effects
classes.role_note: Effective but higher anticholinergic, cardiac and overdose toxicity than newer antidepressants.

classes.name: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs)
classes.mechanism: Irreversibly inhibit MAO-A/B, increasing monoamines
classes.role_note: Specialist treatment-resistant depression option with major food/drug interaction burden.

classes.name: Rapid-acting glutamatergic antidepressant strategies
classes.mechanism: NMDA receptor antagonism and downstream synaptic plasticity effects
classes.role_note: Treatment-resistant depression strategies requiring monitored administration and diagnostic safeguards.

classes.name: Benzodiazepine anxiolytics
classes.mechanism: Positive allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors
classes.role_note: Rapid short-term anxiolysis; dependence, withdrawal, cognitive and fall risks argue against routine long-term use.

classes.name: Non-benzodiazepine anxiolytics
classes.mechanism: Serotonergic, antihistaminic or calcium-channel mechanisms reduce anxiety without classic benzodiazepine pharmacology
classes.role_note: Alternatives/adjuncts for anxiety; onset and evidence differ by agent.

classes.name: Non-benzodiazepine GABA-A hypnotics (Z-drugs)
classes.mechanism: Bind GABA-A benzodiazepine site with relative hypnotic selectivity
classes.role_note: Short-term hypnotics; complex sleep behaviors, next-day impairment and dependence risks remain.

classes.name: Melatonin-receptor sleep agents
classes.mechanism: Activate MT1/MT2 receptors to regulate circadian sleep signaling
classes.role_note: Circadian/sleep-onset focused agents with lower respiratory-depressant burden than GABA hypnotics.

classes.name: Dual orexin receptor antagonists
classes.mechanism: Block orexin OX1/OX2 wake-promoting signaling
classes.role_note: Sleep-onset/maintenance therapy; somnolence and next-day impairment remain important.

classes.name: Second-generation (atypical) antipsychotics
classes.mechanism: D2 and 5-HT2A modulation with agent-specific partial agonism/other receptor effects
classes.role_note: Core schizophrenia/psychosis medicines and some bipolar/augmentation uses; metabolic, prolactin, EPS and QT profiles differ.

classes.name: First-generation (typical) antipsychotics
classes.mechanism: Potent dopamine D2 receptor antagonism
classes.role_note: Effective antipsychotics with higher EPS/tardive dyskinesia burden for many agents.

classes.name: Long-acting injectable antipsychotics
classes.mechanism: Depot formulations provide sustained D2/5-HT2A or partial-agonist exposure
classes.role_note: Adherence-support strategy after oral tolerability/agent-specific loading requirements are addressed.

classes.name: Lithium mood stabilizer
classes.mechanism: Modulates intracellular second-messenger signaling and neurotransmission
classes.role_note: Highly effective mood stabilizer with anti-suicidal evidence but narrow therapeutic index and major renal/thyroid/interactions burden.

classes.name: Antiseizure mood stabilizers
classes.mechanism: Mood stabilization through sodium-channel/GABA/multiple mechanisms
classes.role_note: Valproate, carbamazepine and lamotrigine have different roles in mania vs bipolar depression/maintenance; not interchangeable.

labs.title: Bone • Osteoporosis • Rheumatology Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: BONE REMODELING • GOUT • DMARD • BIOLOGIC • IMMUNE TARGETS
labs.subtitle: Osteoporosis, calcium/vitamin-D, gout/urate, conventional DMARDs, biologic/targeted DMARDs and lupus immunomodulator pharmacology organized for comparative learning.
labs.scientific_boundary: Bone and rheumatology medicines are diagnosis-, fracture-risk-, renal-function-, infection-, vaccination-, pregnancy- and immunologic-phenotype dependent. DMARDs are disease-modifying, not merely analgesics. Biologic/targeted agents require infection/TB/hepatitis screening and monitoring. Denosumab should not be stopped without an antiresorptive transition plan; methotrexate for rheumatic disease is generally weekly, not daily.

classification_notes.Bone_remodeling: Antiresorptive and anabolic osteoporosis therapies act on different sides of bone remodeling; sequence matters in very-high-risk disease.
classification_notes.Urate_science: Acute gout inflammation treatment and long-term urate-lowering therapy are separate decisions; treat-to-target urate strategies require titration.
classification_notes.DMARD_hierarchy: Conventional synthetic, biologic and targeted synthetic DMARDs differ in immune targets, onset, infection risk, monitoring and pregnancy compatibility.
classification_notes.Immune_safety: Before biologic/JAK or potent immunosuppression, review active/latent infection, TB, hepatitis, vaccination, malignancy risk and reproductive plan.
classification_notes.Osteoarthritis_boundary: OA pharmacology is symptom-modifying, not cartilage-regenerating. Topical/oral NSAIDs, acetaminophen, duloxetine and intra-articular corticosteroid have different risk/benefit profiles; exercise, weight management and mechanical interventions remain central.
classification_notes.GIOP: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis risk depends on dose, duration, age, prior fracture and BMD/FRAX context. Bone-protective therapy should be risk-stratified and should not wait for symptomatic fracture in high-risk patients.
classification_notes.DMARD_monitoring: Before biologic/JAK therapy, review TB/hepatitis/infection history and vaccination status. Methotrexate is generally once weekly in rheumatic disease; daily dosing can be fatal.

classes.name: Calcium supplementation
classes.mechanism: Provides elemental calcium substrate for bone mineralization
classes.role_note: Supplement only when dietary intake is inadequate or indicated; total elemental calcium from diet + supplements matters.

classes.name: Vitamin D and active vitamin-D analogues
classes.mechanism: Increase intestinal calcium/phosphate absorption and regulate bone-mineral metabolism
classes.role_note: Correct deficiency and ensure adequacy; active analogues are not interchangeable with nutritional vitamin D and carry higher hypercalcemia risk.

classes.name: Oral bisphosphonates
classes.mechanism: Bind bone hydroxyapatite and inhibit osteoclast-mediated resorption
classes.role_note: Common first-line antiresorptives for many high-fracture-risk patients if renal/GI/oral administration requirements are suitable.

classes.name: IV bisphosphonates
classes.mechanism: Suppress osteoclast function after binding mineralized bone
classes.role_note: Useful when adherence/GI issues limit oral therapy; renal function and acute-phase reaction matter.

classes.name: RANKL inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody blocks RANKL and osteoclast formation/activity
classes.role_note: Potent antiresorptive for high fracture risk; dosing continuity and transition planning are crucial.

classes.name: PTH/PTHrP anabolic agents
classes.mechanism: Intermittent PTH-receptor stimulation promotes osteoblast activity and bone formation
classes.role_note: Anabolic-first option for selected very-high-fracture-risk patients followed by antiresorptive consolidation.

classes.name: Sclerostin inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Blocks sclerostin, increasing bone formation and decreasing resorption
classes.role_note: Time-limited potent therapy for very-high-risk osteoporosis; cardiovascular history is an important selection factor.

classes.name: Selective estrogen receptor modulator
classes.mechanism: Estrogen agonist effect on bone with tissue-selective antagonist/agonist activity
classes.role_note: Vertebral-fracture-focused option in selected postmenopausal women, especially when breast-cancer risk profile is relevant.

classes.name: Calcitonin
classes.mechanism: Inhibits osteoclast resorption through calcitonin receptor
classes.role_note: Limited modern osteoporosis role; sometimes used short-term for analgesia after acute vertebral compression fracture in selected settings.

classes.name: Acute gout anti-inflammatory therapy
classes.mechanism: Suppresses crystal-triggered neutrophil/inflammatory response through microtubule, COX or glucocorticoid pathways
classes.role_note: Treat the flare promptly; agent choice depends on renal/GI/CV risk, interactions and number of joints.

classes.name: Xanthine oxidase inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Reduce uric acid synthesis by inhibiting xanthine oxidase
classes.role_note: Preferred long-term urate-lowering family for many patients; start low and titrate to serum urate target.

classes.name: Uricosurics
classes.mechanism: Increase renal uric-acid excretion by inhibiting tubular urate reabsorption
classes.role_note: Alternative/add-on in selected patients with adequate renal function and no high stone risk.

classes.name: Recombinant uricase
classes.mechanism: Enzymatically converts uric acid to allantoin
classes.role_note: Specialist therapy for severe refractory gout, not routine first-line ULT.

classes.name: Conventional synthetic DMARDs (csDMARDs)
classes.mechanism: Modulate folate/purine/pyrimidine and immune signaling to suppress inflammatory disease
classes.role_note: Core disease-modifying therapy, especially methotrexate for RA; require laboratory and reproductive monitoring.

classes.name: TNF inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Neutralize TNF-α signaling and downstream inflammatory cascades
classes.role_note: Major biologic class across RA/PsA/SpA; screen infection/TB/HBV and avoid certain HF/demyelinating contexts.

classes.name: IL-6 pathway inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Block IL-6 receptor signaling and inflammatory acute-phase pathways
classes.role_note: Effective biologics for RA and selected systemic inflammatory diseases; affect CRP response and lipid/liver/neutrophil monitoring.

classes.name: B-cell depletion therapy
classes.mechanism: Anti-CD20 antibody depletes circulating B cells
classes.role_note: Used in selected RA/vasculitis and off-label/indication-specific autoimmune disease; infusion and infection risks require planning.

classes.name: T-cell costimulation modulator
classes.mechanism: CTLA-4 fusion protein blocks CD80/86–CD28 costimulation
classes.role_note: Biologic RA option with T-cell activation modulation.

classes.name: JAK inhibitors (targeted synthetic DMARDs)
classes.mechanism: Inhibit Janus kinase signaling downstream of multiple cytokine receptors
classes.role_note: Rapid oral targeted DMARDs; regulatory boxed warnings require careful age/CV/VTE/malignancy/infection risk assessment.

classes.name: IL-17 pathway inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Neutralize IL-17A or block IL-17 receptor signaling
classes.role_note: Highly effective for psoriasis/PsA/axial SpA; inflammatory bowel disease context matters.

classes.name: IL-12/23 or IL-23 pathway inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Block IL-12/23 p40 or IL-23 p19 cytokine signaling
classes.role_note: Useful in psoriasis/PsA; generally not core RA therapies.

classes.name: Antimalarial foundation for SLE
classes.mechanism: TLR/endosomal immune modulation and other anti-inflammatory effects
classes.role_note: Hydroxychloroquine is a foundational long-term SLE therapy for most patients unless contraindicated.

classes.name: SLE immunosuppressants
classes.mechanism: Suppress lymphocyte proliferation/DNA synthesis to control organ-threatening autoimmune inflammation
classes.role_note: Used according to organ involvement (e.g., nephritis, CNS, hematologic) and severity; reproductive and infection risks are central.

classes.name: SLE-specific biologics
classes.mechanism: Target B-cell survival factor or type-I interferon receptor
classes.role_note: Add-on disease-modifying biologics for active SLE after standard therapy based on phenotype/organ involvement.

classes.name: Systemic glucocorticoids in rheumatology
classes.mechanism: Genomic/non-genomic glucocorticoid receptor anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects
classes.role_note: Powerful bridge/rescue drugs; use the lowest dose for shortest duration because cumulative toxicity drives infection, diabetes, osteoporosis and CV harm.

classes.name: Osteoarthritis symptom pharmacology (cross-lab reference)
classes.mechanism: Reduces nociceptive/inflammatory signaling through COX inhibition, central analgesia/SNRI pathways, or local intra-articular anti-inflammatory action
classes.target: COX-1/2 • central pain pathways • glucocorticoid receptor
classes.role_note: Symptom-focused OA pharmacology. Drug choice depends on joint, age, GI/CV/renal risk, comorbidity and concurrent therapy; non-pharmacologic management remains foundational.

labs.title: Renal & Urology Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: NEPHROLOGY / UROLOGY CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY LEARNING WORKSPACE
labs.subtitle: CKD/AKI context → cardiorenal protection → diuretics/electrolytes → CKD complications → LUTS/BPH/OAB → stones/ED → mechanism → generic → formulation → adult learning-dose → monitoring/source verification
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning pharmacology only. Kidney and urology prescribing is highly dependent on eGFR, albuminuria, potassium, volume status, acid-base status, dialysis status, obstruction/retention, stone composition, pregnancy and interacting medicines. Displayed doses are adult learning snapshots, not patient-specific prescriptions. AKI, severe electrolyte disturbance, urinary obstruction, priapism and dialysis complications can be emergencies. Verify current guideline/label and local renal-dose resources before prescribing.

classification_notes.renal_dose: Renal function changes exposure to many medicines. eGFR/CrCl method, indication and product label can differ; do not infer a dose from CKD stage alone.
classification_notes.aki_gate: Suspected AKI requires cause/volume/obstruction/nephrotoxin review. Do not use a chronic CKD card as an autonomous AKI treatment protocol.
classification_notes.raas_k_guard: ACEi/ARB/MRA/SGLT2 therapies may be kidney-protective in appropriate CKD but need creatinine/eGFR, potassium, BP and volume monitoring. Hyperkalemia may sometimes be mitigated rather than automatically abandoning beneficial therapy.
classification_notes.diuretic_boundary: Diuretic response depends on GFR, sodium intake, albumin, gut absorption and congestion. Loop-thiazide combinations can produce profound volume/electrolyte depletion and require close monitoring.
classification_notes.electrolyte_emergency: Severe hyperkalemia, symptomatic hyponatremia and severe metabolic acidosis are emergency/specialist contexts. Chronic oral agents must not be confused with immediate membrane-stabilization or shifting therapies.
classification_notes.bph_oab_overlap: Male LUTS can reflect BPH, OAB, urethral stricture, neurogenic bladder, infection or malignancy. Measure retention/PVR and identify red flags before escalating drug therapy.
classification_notes.stone_phenotype: Stone prevention depends on stone analysis and metabolic phenotype. Thiazide, potassium citrate, allopurinol or cystine-directed therapy are not interchangeable universal stone drugs.
classification_notes.ed_nitrate: PDE5 inhibitors are contraindicated with nitrates because of potentially profound hypotension; cardiovascular fitness and interacting alpha-blockers must be reviewed.
classification_notes.dose_boundary: All dose examples are common adult learning snapshots. Renal/hepatic adjustment, dialysis timing, geriatric frailty and product-specific formulation rules must be verified.

classes.name: ACE inhibitors / ARBs in CKD
classes.mechanism: Reduce angiotensin-II signaling, intraglomerular pressure and albuminuria
classes.role_note: Kidney- and CV-protective in appropriate albuminuric CKD; monitor creatinine and potassium after initiation/titration.

classes.name: SGLT2 inhibitors for CKD/cardiorenal protection
classes.mechanism: Reduce proximal tubular glucose/sodium reabsorption and alter tubuloglomerular feedback
classes.role_note: Kidney/CV-protective agents in eligible CKD with or without diabetes depending on indication/label.

classes.name: Nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
classes.mechanism: Selective MR antagonism reduces inflammatory/fibrotic signaling
classes.role_note: Finerenone is used in selected T2D+CKD with albuminuria after potassium/eGFR review.

classes.name: Loop diuretics
classes.mechanism: Block Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in thick ascending limb
classes.role_note: High-potency natriuresis for edema/congestion; dose requirement rises with reduced GFR and resistance.

classes.name: Thiazide / thiazide-like diuretics
classes.mechanism: Block Na-Cl cotransporter in distal convoluted tubule
classes.role_note: BP/edema therapy and selected calcium-stone prevention; can be combined with loop under close monitoring.

classes.name: Steroidal MR antagonists / potassium-sparing diuretics
classes.mechanism: Block aldosterone-mediated sodium retention and potassium excretion
classes.role_note: Useful in HF/resistant HTN/ascites contexts; CKD hyperkalemia risk is central.

classes.name: ENaC blockers
classes.mechanism: Block epithelial sodium channels in collecting duct
classes.role_note: Weak natriuresis; often paired with thiazide to limit hypokalemia; can cause hyperkalemia.

classes.name: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Inhibits proximal tubular bicarbonate reabsorption
classes.role_note: Selected edema/alkalosis/glaucoma/altitude contexts; causes bicarbonate loss.

classes.name: Osmotic diuretic
classes.mechanism: Raises tubular fluid osmolality, limiting water reabsorption
classes.role_note: Hospital/specialist therapy for selected intracranial/intraocular pressure contexts, not routine CKD edema therapy.

classes.name: Chronic potassium binders
classes.mechanism: Bind potassium in GI tract to increase fecal elimination
classes.role_note: Useful for chronic/subacute hyperkalemia mitigation; not substitutes for immediate ECG-directed emergency therapy.

classes.name: Oral alkali therapy
classes.mechanism: Provides bicarbonate/citrate base to correct chronic acid load or alkalinize urine
classes.role_note: Used for selected CKD metabolic acidosis or stone phenotypes after sodium/potassium/volume review.

classes.name: Phosphate binders
classes.mechanism: Bind dietary phosphate in GI tract, reducing absorption
classes.role_note: CKD-MBD therapy is based on serial phosphate/calcium/PTH trends; avoid reflex treatment of a single lab value.

classes.name: Active vitamin-D receptor therapy in CKD-MBD
classes.mechanism: Activates vitamin-D receptor to suppress PTH
classes.role_note: Used selectively for secondary hyperparathyroidism; not interchangeable with routine nutritional vitamin D replacement.

classes.name: Calcimimetics
classes.mechanism: Activate calcium-sensing receptor to suppress PTH secretion
classes.role_note: Secondary hyperparathyroidism therapy especially in dialysis; calcium monitoring is mandatory.

classes.name: Iron replacement in CKD
classes.mechanism: Replaces iron for erythropoiesis
classes.role_note: Iron route and thresholds depend on Hb, ferritin, TSAT, CKD/dialysis status and ESA plan.

classes.name: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents
classes.mechanism: Stimulate erythroid progenitors via erythropoietin receptor
classes.role_note: Used after evaluating/treating iron deficiency and other causes; Hb targets and dosing are deliberately conservative because of CV/thrombotic risk.

classes.name: HIF-prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Stabilizes HIF transcription factors, increasing endogenous EPO and iron availability pathways
classes.role_note: Oral anemia-in-CKD class with jurisdiction/label-specific indications and safety considerations.

classes.name: α1-adrenergic blockers for LUTS/BPH
classes.mechanism: Relax prostatic/bladder-neck smooth muscle
classes.role_note: Rapid symptom improvement in BPH/LUTS but does not reliably shrink prostate or prevent progression alone.

classes.name: 5α-reductase inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Reduce conversion of testosterone to DHT and shrink androgen-dependent prostate tissue
classes.role_note: Best suited to enlarged prostate/progression-risk phenotype; symptom benefit takes months.

classes.name: PDE5 inhibitor for LUTS/BPH
classes.mechanism: Increases cGMP signaling in lower urinary tract smooth muscle
classes.role_note: Tadalafil can address both LUTS/BPH and ED; nitrate contraindication is critical.

classes.name: Antimuscarinics for overactive bladder
classes.mechanism: Block muscarinic detrusor signaling to reduce urgency/frequency
classes.role_note: OAB symptom therapy after behavioral measures; cognitive/anticholinergic burden and retention risk matter.

classes.name: β3-adrenergic agonists for OAB
classes.mechanism: Relax detrusor during storage via β3 receptor activation
classes.role_note: Non-anticholinergic OAB option; BP and interactions differ by agent.

classes.name: Desmopressin for selected nocturnal polyuria
classes.mechanism: V2 receptor agonism increases collecting-duct water reabsorption
classes.role_note: Only for carefully selected nocturnal polyuria/DI contexts; hyponatremia risk can be serious.

classes.name: Thiazides for recurrent calcium-stone phenotype
classes.mechanism: Lower urinary calcium excretion through distal tubular sodium/calcium effects
classes.role_note: Consider only after stone/metabolic evaluation and dietary sodium counseling.

classes.name: Uric-acid / hyperuricosuric stone pharmacology
classes.mechanism: Reduces uric acid production or alkalinizes urine depending phenotype
classes.role_note: Uric-acid stones often depend strongly on urine alkalinization; allopurinol is phenotype-specific rather than universal.

classes.name: Cystinuria-directed thiol therapy
classes.mechanism: Forms more soluble mixed disulfides with cystine
classes.role_note: Specialist therapy after high fluids, sodium/protein measures and urine alkalinization when cystinuria persists.

classes.name: α-blocker medical expulsive therapy context
classes.mechanism: Relaxes ureteral smooth muscle via α1 blockade
classes.role_note: May aid passage of selected ureteral stones; size/location and need for urgent decompression are decisive.

classes.name: PDE5 inhibitors for erectile dysfunction
classes.mechanism: Prevent cGMP degradation and augment nitric-oxide mediated cavernosal smooth-muscle relaxation
classes.role_note: First-line pharmacologic ED class for many patients after cardiovascular/medication review.

classes.name: Prostaglandin E1 erectile therapy
classes.mechanism: Increases cAMP causing cavernosal smooth-muscle relaxation
classes.role_note: Second-line/local ED therapy when oral PDE5 inhibitors are unsuitable or ineffective.

classes.name: Urinary tract analgesic
classes.mechanism: Exerts topical analgesic effect on urinary mucosa after renal excretion
classes.role_note: Short-term symptom relief only; does not treat infection or obstruction.

classes.name: Oral electrolyte replacement
classes.mechanism: Replaces depleted potassium or magnesium stores when oral replacement is appropriate
classes.role_note: Oral replacement is for selected stable deficits; severe/symptomatic disturbances require ECG-aware emergency or monitored protocols.

labs.title: Dermatology Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: DERMATOLOGY RESEARCH & PHARMACOLOGY WORKSPACE
labs.subtitle: Skin/Hair/Nail condition → pharmacologic class → mechanism/target → generic/formulation → monitoring pearl → source verification
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning pharmacology only. Dermatologic treatment depends on morphology, distribution, severity, age, pregnancy, infection status, body-surface area, site-specific potency, prior therapy and diagnostic certainty. Topical corticosteroid potency/site/duration, systemic retinoids, immunosuppressants, JAK inhibitors and biologics require condition- and patient-specific safety verification. Antimicrobial use should avoid unnecessary combinations and follow current guideline/local resistance context.

classification_notes.topical_steroids: Potency, vehicle, body site, age, BSA and duration determine benefit/risk. Face/flexures and children generally require lower potency/shorter exposure.
classification_notes.acne_stewardship: Topical or oral antibiotics should not be used as indefinite monotherapy; benzoyl peroxide/non-antibiotic partners help stewardship where appropriate.
classification_notes.fungal_diagnosis: Dermatophytosis, candidiasis, versicolor and inflammatory mimics are not interchangeable. Avoid empirical steroid-antifungal combination misuse.
classification_notes.systemic_therapy: Systemic retinoids, immunosuppressants, biologics and JAK inhibitors require diagnosis-specific screening, laboratory monitoring and reproductive/infection risk review.
classification_notes.hair_pigment: Alopecia and vitiligo therapies depend on subtype, activity, site, extent and specialist assessment; not all products are approved for every age/site.

classes.name: Topical retinoids
classes.mechanism: Normalize follicular keratinization; comedolytic and anti-inflammatory
classes.role_note: Core acne mechanism; often combined with benzoyl peroxide and/or other agents.

classes.name: Benzoyl peroxide
classes.mechanism: Oxidative antibacterial activity plus mild keratolysis; does not drive classic antibiotic resistance
classes.role_note: Core acne partner, especially when topical/oral antibiotics are used.

classes.name: Topical acne antibacterials
classes.mechanism: Reduce C. acnes and inflammation
classes.target: Bacterial protein synthesis / follicular bacterial burden
classes.role_note: Avoid topical-antibiotic monotherapy; pair with benzoyl peroxide where guideline/label appropriate.

classes.name: Azelaic acid / topical anti-inflammatory acne agents
classes.mechanism: Antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and keratinization-modifying effects
classes.role_note: Useful non-antibiotic option; azelaic acid also relevant to dyspigmentation/rosacea.

classes.name: Oral tetracycline-class acne therapy
classes.mechanism: Anti-inflammatory + 30S ribosomal antibacterial activity
classes.role_note: Moderate-severe inflammatory acne; limit duration and combine with non-antibiotic topical therapy.

classes.name: Systemic acne disease-modifying therapy
classes.mechanism: Sebaceous suppression/retinoid signaling or androgen modulation
classes.role_note: Severe/scarring/refractory acne or selected hormonally mediated acne; specialist monitoring.

classes.name: Emollients / barrier repair
classes.mechanism: Reduce transepidermal water loss and restore skin barrier
classes.role_note: Foundation therapy for eczema/xerosis; product choice based on tolerability and site.

classes.name: Low-potency topical corticosteroids
classes.mechanism: Genomic anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive glucocorticoid signaling
classes.role_note: Face/flexural/child-sensitive sites often require lower potency and short courses.

classes.name: Medium-potency topical corticosteroids
classes.mechanism: Genomic anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive glucocorticoid signaling
classes.role_note: Common trunk/limb inflammatory-dermatosis tier; site/duration matter.

classes.name: High/super-high potency topical corticosteroids
classes.mechanism: Genomic anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive glucocorticoid signaling
classes.role_note: Thick plaques/palms/soles or severe disease; short specialist-directed courses.

classes.name: Topical calcineurin inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Calcineurin inhibition → reduced T-cell cytokine transcription
classes.role_note: Steroid-sparing therapy, especially sensitive sites; off-label contexts require verification.

classes.name: Topical PDE4 / JAK / AhR-pathway agents
classes.mechanism: Reduce inflammatory signaling via PDE4, JAK or aryl-hydrocarbon receptor pathways
classes.role_note: Newer nonsteroidal options; exact age/site/BSA approvals differ by product.

classes.name: Second-generation H1 antihistamines
classes.mechanism: Peripheral H1 receptor inverse agonism
classes.role_note: Core symptomatic urticaria therapy; escalation strategy is diagnosis-specific.

classes.name: Advanced chronic urticaria therapy
classes.mechanism: IgE neutralization or downstream immunomodulation
classes.role_note: For chronic spontaneous urticaria inadequately controlled with antihistamine strategy; specialist use.

classes.name: Topical azole antifungals
classes.mechanism: Inhibit fungal ergosterol synthesis via 14α-demethylase
classes.role_note: Tinea/candidal/versicolor contexts; site and organism matter.

classes.name: Allylamine antifungals
classes.mechanism: Inhibit squalene epoxidase → ergosterol depletion
classes.role_note: Highly active against dermatophytes; oral therapy may be needed for selected nail/extensive disease.

classes.name: Systemic azole antifungals
classes.mechanism: Inhibit fungal ergosterol synthesis via CYP51
classes.role_note: Selected extensive/refractory fungal disease; interaction/hepatic risk important.

classes.name: Scabicides
classes.mechanism: Neurotoxic/paralytic action against Sarcoptes scabiei
classes.target: Mite sodium/chloride channels or glutamate-gated chloride channels

classes.name: Topical antibacterials for localized bacterial skin disease
classes.mechanism: Inhibit bacterial protein synthesis
classes.role_note: Use for limited appropriate lesions; avoid unnecessary prolonged topical-antibiotic exposure.

classes.name: Herpesvirus antivirals
classes.mechanism: Inhibit viral DNA polymerase after phosphorylation
classes.role_note: HSV/zoster treatment depends on syndrome, timing, immune status and renal function.

classes.name: Common wart pharmacotherapy
classes.mechanism: Keratolysis or local immune activation
classes.role_note: Many warts resolve spontaneously; site and diagnosis determine therapy.

classes.name: Psoriasis topical nonsteroid agents
classes.mechanism: Normalize keratinocyte differentiation or reduce inflammatory signaling
classes.role_note: Localized plaque/scalp/intertriginous psoriasis options; site-specific selection.

classes.name: Conventional systemic psoriasis therapy
classes.mechanism: Immune-cell suppression, retinoid signaling or PDE4 inhibition
classes.role_note: Moderate-severe disease; laboratory, pregnancy and infection risk guide choice.

classes.name: TNF inhibitors for psoriasis
classes.mechanism: Neutralize TNF-α inflammatory signaling
classes.role_note: Moderate-severe psoriasis/PsA; TB/HBV and infection screening before therapy.

classes.name: IL-17 pathway inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Block IL-17A or IL-17 receptor signaling
classes.role_note: Highly effective psoriasis biologic class; candidiasis/IBD context relevant.

classes.name: IL-23 / IL-12-23 inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Block p19 IL-23 or p40 IL-12/23 signaling
classes.role_note: Long-interval biologic options for moderate-severe plaque psoriasis.

classes.name: Systemic atopic-dermatitis targeted therapy
classes.mechanism: Block type-2 cytokines or JAK signaling
classes.role_note: Moderate-severe AD inadequately controlled by topical therapy; agent-specific age and safety criteria.

classes.name: Rosacea pharmacotherapy
classes.mechanism: Anti-inflammatory, antiparasitic or vasoconstrictor mechanisms
classes.role_note: Phenotype-directed treatment: papulopustular vs erythema vs ocular disease.

classes.name: Vitiligo pharmacotherapy
classes.mechanism: Local immunomodulation to suppress depigmenting immune activity and support repigmentation
classes.role_note: Treatment depends on activity, site, BSA and phototherapy availability.

classes.name: Androgenetic alopecia therapy
classes.mechanism: Prolong anagen or reduce DHT signaling
classes.role_note: Pattern hair loss therapy; diagnosis and sex-specific risk counseling important.

classes.name: Alopecia areata immunomodulatory therapy
classes.mechanism: Suppress autoimmune attack on hair follicle
classes.role_note: Patchy disease vs extensive disease require different strategy; systemic JAK therapy is specialist-led.

classes.name: Melasma / hyperpigmentation topical therapy
classes.mechanism: Reduce melanogenesis or accelerate pigment turnover
classes.role_note: Sun protection is foundational; avoid prolonged unsupervised hydroquinone/steroid-combination use.

classes.name: Seborrheic dermatitis therapy
classes.mechanism: Reduce Malassezia burden and local inflammation
classes.role_note: Scalp/face therapy combines antifungal and short anti-inflammatory courses when needed.

labs.title: GI • Bowel • Liver Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: Gastroenterology • Bowel Pharmacology • Hepatology Research Workspace
labs.subtitle: Nausea/constipation/diarrhea/IBS → IBD → pancreas → cirrhosis/portal HTN → cholestatic & metabolic liver pharmacology
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning pharmacology only. Acid-peptic/H. pylori therapy remains in the dedicated Acid-Peptic Lab. GI symptoms require diagnosis and red-flag assessment before symptomatic drugs. IBD biologics/small molecules, cirrhosis vasoactive therapy, HRS treatment, PBC second-line agents and MASH therapies are specialist/high-risk. Exact indication, severity, formulation, dose, duration, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy, infection screening, interactions and current guideline/label must be verified.
classification_notes: Symptom control is separated from disease-modifying therapy.
IBD classes are organized by mechanism; positioning changes with severity, prior exposure and current guidelines.
Cirrhosis/portal-hypertension drugs are not routine OPD equivalents of their cardiovascular uses.
Obeticholic acid is intentionally excluded from active PBC options because its U.S. PBC accelerated-approval indication was withdrawn in 2025.
Hepatitis B/C antivirals are reserved for the future Antiviral/Anti-infective Lab to avoid duplication.

classes.name: 5-HT3 receptor antagonist antiemetics
classes.mechanism: Block serotonin 5-HT3 signaling in vagal afferents and the vomiting pathway
classes.role_note: Antiemetic class; indication and QT/electrolyte context matter.

classes.name: Dopamine-antagonist antiemetic / prokinetic agents
classes.mechanism: D2 antagonism; metoclopramide also enhances upper-GI motility through serotonergic actions
classes.role_note: Useful in selected nausea/gastroparesis contexts; neurologic and cardiac adverse effects limit use.

classes.name: NK1 receptor antagonist antiemetics
classes.mechanism: Block substance-P signaling in central emetic pathways
classes.role_note: Primarily protocol-driven prevention of highly emetogenic nausea/vomiting.

classes.name: H1 / anticholinergic antiemetic agents
classes.mechanism: Suppress vestibular H1 and muscarinic signaling
classes.role_note: Motion/vestibular-predominant nausea; sedation and anticholinergic burden matter.

classes.name: Oral rehydration solution (ORS)
classes.mechanism: Glucose-sodium cotransport facilitates intestinal sodium and water absorption
classes.role_note: Foundational rehydration therapy for diarrheal fluid loss; not an antidiarrheal.

classes.name: Bulk-forming fiber laxatives
classes.mechanism: Increase stool water/bulk and support colonic transit
classes.role_note: Useful for selected constipation/IBS patients when hydration and obstruction risk are considered.

classes.name: Osmotic laxatives
classes.mechanism: Retain luminal water to soften stool and increase bowel movement frequency
classes.role_note: Core constipation pharmacology; renal/electrolyte context affects agent choice.

classes.name: Stimulant laxatives
classes.mechanism: Stimulate colonic motility and secretion
classes.role_note: Effective rescue/short-course or scheduled therapy depending context.

classes.name: Stool softeners
classes.mechanism: Surfactant effect facilitates mixing of water/fat into stool
classes.role_note: Commonly used but comparatively limited efficacy evidence for CIC.

classes.name: Chloride-channel secretagogue
classes.mechanism: Activates intestinal chloride secretion to increase fluid and transit
classes.role_note: Prescription constipation/IBS-C option.

classes.name: Guanylate cyclase-C agonists
classes.mechanism: Increase intestinal cGMP, chloride/bicarbonate secretion and transit
classes.role_note: High-evidence prescription options for CIC/IBS-C.

classes.name: Selective 5-HT4 prokinetic
classes.mechanism: Enhances enteric cholinergic signaling and colonic motility
classes.role_note: Prescription prokinetic option for CIC.

classes.name: Intestinal NHE3 inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Reduces intestinal sodium absorption, increasing luminal water and accelerating transit
classes.role_note: IBS-C targeted therapy.

classes.name: Peripherally acting µ-opioid receptor antagonists (PAMORAs)
classes.mechanism: Block peripheral GI µ-opioid effects while minimizing central analgesia reversal
classes.role_note: Targeted opioid-induced constipation therapy after standard laxative assessment.

classes.name: Peripheral opioid antidiarrheals
classes.mechanism: Reduce intestinal propulsive motility and secretion
classes.role_note: Symptomatic diarrhea control only after red flags/infectious/inflammatory causes are considered.

classes.name: Bile-acid sequestrants for bile-acid diarrhea
classes.mechanism: Bind intestinal bile acids
classes.role_note: Useful when bile-acid excess contributes to diarrhea; also used for cholestatic pruritus in liver disease.

classes.name: Gut-selective rifamycin for IBS-D
classes.mechanism: Minimally absorbed rifamycin alters gut microbial activity
classes.role_note: Short-course IBS-D therapy in selected adults; retreatment may be label-supported.

classes.name: Selective 5-HT3 antagonist for severe IBS-D
classes.mechanism: Reduces visceral signaling and slows colonic transit
classes.role_note: Restricted/high-risk IBS-D option for selected patients.

classes.name: Mixed opioid-receptor modulator for IBS-D
classes.mechanism: µ- and κ-opioid receptor agonism with δ antagonism in the gut
classes.role_note: IBS-D therapy with important pancreatitis/gallbladder contraindications.

classes.name: GI antispasmodics / smooth-muscle relaxants
classes.mechanism: Reduce intestinal smooth-muscle spasm through antimuscarinic or direct mechanisms
classes.role_note: Symptom-directed abdominal cramp/spasm therapy; evidence and availability vary.

classes.name: 5-aminosalicylates (5-ASA)
classes.mechanism: Topical mucosal anti-inflammatory effects through multiple eicosanoid/NF-κB pathways
classes.role_note: Core mild-to-moderate UC class; role in Crohn disease is much more limited.

classes.name: Corticosteroids for IBD induction
classes.mechanism: Broad glucocorticoid anti-inflammatory effects
classes.role_note: Induction/rescue—not maintenance—therapy; minimize systemic steroid exposure.

classes.name: Thiopurine immunomodulators
classes.mechanism: Inhibit purine synthesis and lymphocyte proliferation
classes.role_note: Maintenance/steroid-sparing role in selected IBD patients; not rapid induction monotherapy.

classes.name: Methotrexate immunomodulation in Crohn disease
classes.mechanism: Folate-pathway and adenosine-mediated immunomodulation
classes.role_note: Selected Crohn disease maintenance/steroid-sparing option; pregnancy contraindication.

classes.name: Anti-TNF biologics for IBD
classes.mechanism: Neutralize tumor necrosis factor-α
classes.role_note: Advanced therapy for moderate-to-severe IBD; therapeutic drug monitoring may be used contextually.

classes.name: Gut-selective anti-integrin biologic
classes.mechanism: Blocks α4β7 integrin-mediated lymphocyte trafficking to gut
classes.role_note: Gut-selective advanced IBD therapy.

classes.name: IL-12/23 and IL-23 pathway biologics
classes.mechanism: Block p40 or p19 cytokine subunits to reduce Th1/Th17 inflammation
classes.role_note: Major contemporary IBD biologic pathway; induction and maintenance differ by agent/indication.

classes.name: JAK inhibitors for IBD
classes.mechanism: Inhibit Janus kinase signaling downstream of multiple cytokines
classes.role_note: Rapid oral advanced therapy with boxed-warning considerations.

classes.name: S1P receptor modulators for UC
classes.mechanism: Sequester lymphocytes in lymphoid tissue by modulating S1P receptors
classes.role_note: Oral UC advanced therapy with cardiac/ophthalmic and infection considerations.

classes.name: Pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT)
classes.mechanism: Replaces pancreatic lipase/protease/amylase in the intestinal lumen
classes.role_note: Foundation of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency treatment; dose is lipase-unit and meal based.

classes.name: Hepatic encephalopathy ammonia-reduction therapy
classes.mechanism: Reduce intestinal ammonia generation/absorption through catharsis and gut-microbial effects
classes.role_note: Core pharmacologic strategy for overt/recurrent hepatic encephalopathy.

classes.name: Cirrhotic ascites diuretic strategy
classes.mechanism: Aldosterone antagonism plus loop diuresis mobilizes sodium/water
classes.role_note: Standard cirrhotic ascites pharmacology after sodium strategy and severity assessment.

classes.name: Nonselective beta-blockers for portal hypertension
classes.mechanism: β1 blockade reduces cardiac output; β2 blockade reduces splanchnic inflow; carvedilol adds α1 blockade
classes.role_note: Primary/secondary portal-hypertension prophylaxis in selected cirrhosis patients; BP and decompensation status are critical.

classes.name: Vasoactive therapy for acute variceal hemorrhage
classes.mechanism: Reduces splanchnic blood flow and portal pressure
classes.role_note: Emergency hospital therapy alongside resuscitation, endoscopy and antibiotic strategy—not OPD self-treatment.

classes.name: Hepatorenal syndrome–AKI vasoconstrictor + albumin strategy
classes.mechanism: Vasoconstriction reverses splanchnic vasodilation while albumin supports effective arterial volume
classes.target: Vasopressin V1 receptors + plasma oncotic expansion
classes.role_note: Hospital/specialist HRS-AKI therapy after diagnostic confirmation and volume/infection assessment.

classes.name: Ursodeoxycholic acid for PBC
classes.mechanism: Hydrophilic bile acid improves bile flow and reduces toxic bile-acid effects
classes.role_note: First-line disease-modifying therapy for primary biliary cholangitis.

classes.name: Newer PPAR agonists for PBC
classes.mechanism: Modulate PPAR signaling to reduce cholestatic injury and bile-acid synthesis pathways
classes.role_note: Second-line PBC options after inadequate UDCA response or intolerance; accelerated-approval/specialist context.

classes.name: Cholestatic-pruritus pharmacotherapy
classes.mechanism: Uses bile-acid binding, hepatic enzyme induction, opioid antagonism or serotonergic modulation
classes.role_note: Stepwise symptom therapy; space bile-acid binders from other medicines and monitor specialist agents.

classes.name: Disease-directed pharmacotherapy for noncirrhotic MASH with F2–F3 fibrosis
classes.mechanism: Targets hepatic thyroid-hormone signaling or GLP-1 pathways plus metabolic weight-loss effects
classes.role_note: Current FDA-approved MASH options are stage- and label-specific; lifestyle/metabolic risk management remains foundational.

classes.name: Corticosteroid therapy for severe alcohol-associated hepatitis
classes.mechanism: Suppresses inflammatory cytokine signaling in selected severe alcohol-associated hepatitis
classes.role_note: Short-course specialist therapy only after severity scoring and contraindication/infection assessment.

labs.title: Antifungal • Antiviral • Antiparasitic Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: NON-BACTERIAL ANTI-INFECTIVE PHARMACOLOGY WORKSPACE
labs.subtitle: Pathogen domain → pharmacologic class → mechanism/target → generic/formulation → practical role → monitoring pearl → source verification
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning pharmacology only. Antifungal, antiviral and antiparasitic therapy depends on organism/species, infection site, severity, immune status, pregnancy, age/weight, renal/hepatic function, resistance/susceptibility, drug interactions, local epidemiology and current public-health/specialty guidance. HIV/HBV/HCV, invasive mycoses, malaria, visceral leishmaniasis, severe strongyloidiasis and other complex infections require guideline- and specialist-controlled regimens. Do not infer a treatment regimen from a class card alone.
classification_notes: Fungal therapy is separated into superficial/mucosal vs invasive/systemic disease and by target class (azole, echinocandin, polyene, allylamine, other).
Antiviral therapy is separated by virus family and mechanism; HIV and HCV are regimen-based, not single-drug prescribing problems.
Antiparasitic therapy is separated into helminths, intestinal protozoa, malaria and tissue/vector-borne protozoa.
Pregnancy, G6PD status, QT risk, CYP interactions and renal/hepatic function can materially alter drug choice.
Species identification, resistance/susceptibility and public-health guidance supersede broad learning labels.

classes.name: Topical azole antifungals
classes.mechanism: Inhibit fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase and ergosterol synthesis
classes.role_note: High-use topical class for dermatophyte and selected Candida infections; site/diagnosis matter.

classes.name: Allylamine antifungals
classes.mechanism: Inhibit squalene epoxidase, reducing ergosterol and accumulating squalene
classes.role_note: Particularly important for dermatophytes; oral terbinafine is a systemic onychomycosis option.

classes.name: Polyene antifungals
classes.mechanism: Bind fungal ergosterol and disrupt membrane integrity
classes.role_note: Nystatin is local/mucosal; amphotericin B is a major systemic antifungal with substantial toxicity/infusion considerations.

classes.name: Systemic triazoles — fluconazole / itraconazole
classes.mechanism: Inhibit CYP51-dependent ergosterol synthesis
classes.role_note: High-use systemic azoles with very different spectra, PK and interaction profiles.

classes.name: Mold-active triazoles
classes.mechanism: Inhibit fungal CYP51 with expanded mold activity
classes.role_note: Specialist class for invasive mold disease; drug levels/interactions may matter.

classes.name: Echinocandins
classes.mechanism: Inhibit beta-(1,3)-D-glucan synthesis in fungal cell wall
classes.role_note: Core invasive-Candida class; limited oral availability means IV use.

classes.name: Other systemic/local antifungals
classes.mechanism: Distinct mechanisms outside major azole/polyene/echinocandin groups
classes.target: DNA/RNA synthesis or fungal membrane/cell wall targets
classes.role_note: Useful niche or adjunct agents; mechanism and toxicity differ substantially.

classes.name: HSV/VZV nucleoside analogues
classes.mechanism: Viral thymidine-kinase activation followed by inhibition of viral DNA polymerase
classes.role_note: Core herpes simplex and zoster antivirals; timing and renal function matter.

classes.name: CMV DNA-polymerase inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Inhibit CMV DNA synthesis through nucleoside/nucleotide analog or pyrophosphate mechanisms
classes.role_note: Specialist CMV treatment/toxicity class.

classes.name: CMV terminase inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Inhibits CMV DNA terminase complex, preventing viral DNA processing/packaging
classes.role_note: Primarily CMV prophylaxis in defined transplant contexts; not interchangeable with treatment regimens.

classes.name: Influenza neuraminidase inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Block release of progeny influenza virions
classes.role_note: Treatment/prophylaxis class; benefit greatest when started early, but severe/high-risk illness may warrant later treatment.

classes.name: Influenza cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Blocks cap-snatching needed for influenza viral mRNA synthesis
classes.role_note: Single-dose oral option for selected uncomplicated influenza; resistance/pregnancy contexts matter.

classes.name: Direct-acting COVID-19 antivirals
classes.mechanism: Inhibit SARS-CoV-2 protease or RNA-dependent RNA polymerase
classes.role_note: Early outpatient or inpatient antiviral therapy is indication/risk-window specific; interaction screening is critical.

classes.name: HBV nucleos(t)ide analogues
classes.mechanism: Suppress hepatitis B reverse-transcriptase/DNA-polymerase activity
classes.role_note: Preferred long-term oral suppressive therapy in eligible chronic HBV; treatment eligibility and stopping are guideline controlled.

classes.name: HCV direct-acting antiviral combinations
classes.mechanism: Block HCV protease, NS5A replication complex and/or NS5B polymerase
classes.role_note: HCV is treated with complete combination regimens selected by cirrhosis, prior treatment, interactions and other factors.

classes.name: HIV NRTI/NtRTI backbone agents
classes.mechanism: Terminate or disrupt HIV reverse-transcription after intracellular phosphorylation
classes.role_note: Backbone agents used only within complete ART regimens; resistance and HBV coinfection matter.

classes.name: HIV integrase strand-transfer inhibitors (INSTIs)
classes.mechanism: Block strand transfer of viral DNA into host genome
classes.role_note: Preferred-anchor class in many modern ART regimens; cation interactions and resistance history matter.

classes.name: HIV NNRTI / protease-inhibitor anchors
classes.mechanism: Noncompetitive reverse-transcriptase inhibition or protease inhibition
classes.role_note: Alternative/selected ART anchors with major interaction and resistance considerations.

classes.name: HIV entry/fusion/attachment/capsid agents
classes.mechanism: Block CCR5, fusion, attachment/post-attachment or capsid functions
classes.role_note: Specialist/resistance-context HIV agents; not routine standalone therapy.

classes.name: Benzimidazole anthelmintics
classes.mechanism: Bind parasite beta-tubulin and inhibit microtubule function/glucose uptake
classes.role_note: High-use deworming class; organism and pregnancy/age context determine regimen.

classes.name: Depolarizing neuromuscular anthelmintic
classes.mechanism: Causes persistent parasite neuromuscular depolarization/paralysis
classes.role_note: Common pinworm/selected intestinal-nematode agent.

classes.name: Macrocyclic lactone antiparasitic
classes.mechanism: Binds glutamate-gated chloride channels causing parasite paralysis/death
classes.role_note: Key drug for strongyloidiasis; also used in selected ectoparasitic/filarial contexts.

classes.name: Praziquantel — trematode/cestode therapy
classes.mechanism: Increases parasite membrane calcium permeability causing contraction and tegument damage
classes.role_note: Core schistosomiasis and several cestode/trematode treatments; weight/species-specific dosing.

classes.name: Fasciolicide
classes.mechanism: Disrupts parasite microtubule-dependent processes
classes.role_note: Fasciola hepatica/gigantica-specific therapy.

classes.name: Filarial therapies
classes.mechanism: Reduce microfilariae/adult-worm burden via parasite-specific mechanisms
classes.role_note: Public-health/specialist regimens vary by species and geographic Loa loa risk.

classes.name: Nitroimidazole antiprotozoals
classes.mechanism: Reduced metabolites damage DNA in susceptible anaerobic protozoa
classes.role_note: High-use giardiasis/amebiasis/trichomoniasis class; luminal follow-on therapy is needed for invasive E. histolytica.

classes.name: Luminal amebicides
classes.mechanism: Act within intestinal lumen against Entamoeba cysts/trophozoites
classes.role_note: Used after tissue-active treatment for invasive amebiasis or for selected luminal infection.

classes.name: Nitazoxanide / pyruvate-ferredoxin pathway inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Interferes with pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase-dependent metabolism in susceptible protozoa
classes.role_note: Option for selected Giardia/Cryptosporidium contexts; host immune status matters.

classes.name: Artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs)
classes.mechanism: Rapid artemisinin parasite killing plus longer-acting partner drug
classes.role_note: WHO core strategy for uncomplicated falciparum malaria; national resistance/species guidance determines regimen.

classes.name: Severe-malaria parenteral therapy
classes.mechanism: Rapid artemisinin activity against blood-stage Plasmodium
classes.role_note: Emergency specialist treatment; transition to complete oral ACT after stabilization per guideline.

classes.name: 8-aminoquinolines for radical cure/transmission blocking
classes.mechanism: Target dormant liver hypnozoites and/or gametocytes
classes.role_note: Primaquine/tafenoquine require quantitative G6PD-aware use; pregnancy restrictions are critical.

classes.name: Other antimalarial agents
classes.mechanism: Diverse inhibition of parasite folate, mitochondrial or heme-related pathways
classes.role_note: Use depends on species, resistance geography, prophylaxis vs treatment and pregnancy.

classes.name: Antileishmanial therapies
classes.mechanism: Disrupt parasite membrane/metabolism or intracellular survival through diverse mechanisms
classes.role_note: Species/geographic syndrome and visceral vs cutaneous disease determine regimen; specialist care common.

classes.name: Toxoplasmosis combination therapy
classes.mechanism: Sequential folate-pathway inhibition against Toxoplasma gondii
classes.role_note: CNS/ocular/congenital and HIV-associated disease require specialist combination regimens.

labs.title: Hematology • Anemia • Hematinics Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: HEMATOLOGY • ANEMIA • HEMATINICS RESEARCH WORKSPACE
labs.subtitle: Phenotype/cause → hematinic or hematology class → mechanism/target → generic/formulation → learning dose → monitoring → source verification
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning pharmacology only. Anemia is a diagnosis pattern, not a single treatment indication. Confirm cause (iron deficiency, B12/folate deficiency, CKD/inflammation, blood loss, hemolysis, marrow disease, hemoglobinopathy or mixed causes) before therapy. Transfusion, ESA/HIF-PHI, IV iron, ITP, sickle cell, thalassemia and hemostatic products require patient-specific thresholds, specialist protocols, current labeling and laboratory monitoring. Do not infer transfusion need or a disease-modifying regimen from a class card alone.
classification_notes: Iron therapy is separated into oral elemental-iron strategies and IV iron complexes; product names are not mg-for-mg interchangeable.
B12 deficiency must be considered before isolated folate replacement when macrocytosis/neurologic risk exists.
CKD anemia is separated into iron optimization, ESA and HIF-PHI pathways under KDIGO 2026; correctable causes should be addressed first.
Sickle-cell and thalassemia therapies are disease-modifying/specialist modules, not generic anemia treatment.
RBC/platelet/plasma/cryoprecipitate cards are transfusion-support concepts; decisions depend on symptoms, bleeding, comorbidity, procedure and institutional blood-bank policy.
Voxelotor is not listed as an active sickle-cell option because FDA announced its market withdrawal in September 2024 for safety concerns.

classes.mechanism: Deliver iron directly to reticuloendothelial/transferrin pathways, bypassing intestinal absorption

classes.role_note: Public-health prophylaxis is distinct from treatment of established anemia.

classes.name: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs)
classes.mechanism: Activate erythropoietin receptor signaling to stimulate erythroid progenitors
classes.role_note: CKD and selected oncology/anemia contexts; initiation and Hb targets are protocol controlled.

classes.name: HIF-prolyl hydroxylase inhibitors (HIF-PHI)
classes.mechanism: Stabilize hypoxia-inducible factor, increasing endogenous EPO signaling and altering iron metabolism
classes.role_note: Oral CKD-anemia class with country/label restrictions; not interchangeable across jurisdictions.

classes.name: Sickle-cell disease-modifying pharmacotherapy
classes.mechanism: Reduces HbS polymerization-related complications or vaso-occlusive biology through distinct pathways
classes.target: HbF induction / redox support / P-selectin adhesion
classes.role_note: Disease-modifying therapy for confirmed sickle-cell disease; hematology follow-up is required.

classes.name: Iron chelation therapy
classes.mechanism: Binds excess iron to increase excretion and reduce transfusional iron toxicity
classes.role_note: For transfusion-dependent iron overload and selected chronic iron-loading conditions; guided by ferritin, transfusion burden and organ iron assessment.

classes.name: Erythroid maturation agents
classes.mechanism: Enhance late-stage erythroid maturation by modifying TGF-beta superfamily signaling
classes.target: Activin receptor ligand trap / SMAD pathway
classes.role_note: Specialist therapy for selected transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia and other approved anemia indications.

classes.name: ITP first-line corticosteroid therapy
classes.mechanism: Reduces immune-mediated platelet destruction and autoantibody activity
classes.role_note: Short-course first-line option in selected adults with ITP; observation may be appropriate depending on platelet count/bleeding.

classes.name: Rapid immune modulation for ITP
classes.mechanism: Temporarily reduces Fc-mediated platelet clearance / immune destruction
classes.role_note: Used when rapid platelet rise is required or in specific bleeding/procedure contexts.

classes.name: Thrombopoietin receptor agonists (TPO-RAs)
classes.mechanism: Stimulate megakaryocyte proliferation and platelet production via c-Mpl
classes.role_note: Second-line/chronic ITP and selected thrombocytopenia indications; agents differ in food/interactions and indication.

classes.name: Spleen tyrosine kinase (SYK) inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Reduces Fc-receptor-mediated platelet destruction by inhibiting SYK signaling
classes.role_note: Second-line chronic ITP option after insufficient response to prior therapy.

classes.name: B-cell-directed immune therapy
classes.mechanism: Depletes CD20-positive B cells, reducing autoantibody-producing precursors
classes.role_note: Off-label/second-line immune strategy in ITP and other immune hematologic disorders.

classes.name: Granulocyte colony-stimulating factors (G-CSF)
classes.mechanism: Stimulate neutrophil progenitor proliferation/differentiation and release
classes.role_note: Prevention/treatment of selected chemotherapy- or disease-associated neutropenia; oncology/hematology protocol controlled.

classes.name: Antifibrinolytics
classes.mechanism: Block plasminogen activation or plasmin binding, reducing fibrin clot breakdown
classes.role_note: Useful for selected mucosal, surgical, trauma and bleeding contexts; thrombotic and urinary-tract considerations matter.

classes.name: Vitamin K replacement / VKA reversal support
classes.mechanism: Restores hepatic gamma-carboxylation of vitamin-K-dependent clotting factors
classes.target: Vitamin K epoxide cycle / factors II, VII, IX, X
classes.role_note: For vitamin-K deficiency and protocol-based warfarin reversal; urgent bleeding may also require factor replacement.

classes.name: Desmopressin hemostatic therapy
classes.mechanism: Releases endogenous von Willebrand factor and factor VIII from endothelial stores
classes.role_note: Selected mild hemophilia A, type 1 von Willebrand disease and platelet-dysfunction contexts after response assessment.

classes.name: Coagulation factor concentrates / PCC
classes.mechanism: Replace deficient vitamin-K-dependent or specific clotting factors
classes.role_note: Emergency/specialist factor replacement for major bleeding, reversal or inherited factor deficiency.

classes.name: Fibrinogen replacement
classes.mechanism: Restores fibrinogen substrate required for stable clot formation
classes.role_note: For documented hypofibrinogenemia/afibrinogenemia or major bleeding protocols.

classes.name: Red blood cell transfusion support
classes.mechanism: Increases circulating red-cell mass and oxygen-carrying capacity
classes.role_note: Not a hematinic substitute. Use patient-blood-management principles and individualized transfusion thresholds.

classes.name: Platelet transfusion support
classes.mechanism: Raises circulating platelet mass to improve primary hemostasis when indicated
classes.role_note: Indication depends on bleeding, procedure, cause of thrombocytopenia and expected platelet survival; routine ITP transfusion is generally not a durable strategy.

classes.name: Plasma transfusion support
classes.mechanism: Replaces multiple coagulation factors
classes.role_note: For selected bleeding/coagulopathy contexts; not for simple volume expansion.

classes.name: Terminal/complement-pathway inhibitors for PNH
classes.mechanism: Reduce complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis by blocking C5 or proximal complement
classes.role_note: Highly specialized PNH disease-modifying therapy requiring meningococcal/infection-risk management and hematology oversight.

classes.name: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia immune therapy
classes.mechanism: Suppresses autoantibody-mediated red-cell destruction
classes.role_note: Cause/subtype-directed therapy; warm and cold AIHA pathways differ.

classes.name: Immune TTP targeted therapy
classes.mechanism: Blocks von Willebrand factor–platelet interaction while immune therapy and plasma exchange address ADAMTS13 autoimmunity
classes.target: vWF A1 domain / platelet GPIb interaction
classes.role_note: Emergency specialist module; plasma exchange + immunosuppression remain core context.

classes.name: Supportive therapy in chronic hemolysis
classes.mechanism: Replaces nutrients consumed by accelerated erythropoiesis and addresses cause-specific needs
classes.role_note: Supportive, not disease-curative; use only when deficiency/high turnover warrants it.
