labs.title: Fluids • Electrolytes • Nutrition Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: FLUIDS • ELECTROLYTES • NUTRITION RESEARCH WORKSPACE
labs.subtitle: Clinical problem → fluid/electrolyte/nutrition class → physiologic target → formulation/route → learning dose/concentration → monitoring → source verification
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning CDS only. Fluid, electrolyte and nutrition therapy can cause rapid harm when indication, volume status, tonicity, renal function, acid-base status, ECG, glucose and ongoing losses are not assessed. No card is an automatic correction protocol. Severe sodium disorders, potassium emergencies, symptomatic hypocalcemia/hypomagnesemia, refeeding syndrome, parenteral nutrition and hypertonic saline require monitored settings and current institutional/guideline protocols. Never infer an IV rate or concentration from a generic class card alone.
classification_notes: Oral/enteral replacement is preferred when feasible; IV fluid therapy should be used only when needs cannot be met orally/enterally and stopped as soon as possible.
Crystalloids are separated by tonicity/composition because chloride load, potassium/calcium content and acid-base effects differ.
Hyponatremia and hypernatremia are water-balance disorders; treatment depends on symptoms, chronicity, volume status and cause, not the sodium value alone.
Potassium, magnesium, calcium and phosphate replacement require route-, concentration-, renal-function- and monitoring-specific verification. Potassium must never be given as an IV push.
Refeeding-risk patients need thiamine plus careful calorie/electrolyte advancement and monitoring rather than immediate full feeding.
Enteral and parenteral nutrition cards are formulation frameworks, not ready-made prescriptions; protein/energy/fluid/electrolyte targets are patient-specific.

classes.name: Reduced-osmolarity oral rehydration solution (ORS)
classes.mechanism: Coupled intestinal sodium-glucose transport promotes water and electrolyte absorption
classes.target: SGLT1-mediated sodium-glucose co-transport in small intestine
classes.role_note: Foundation for oral rehydration in diarrheal fluid loss when oral therapy is feasible.

classes.name: 0.9% sodium chloride crystalloid
classes.mechanism: Expands extracellular/intravascular volume with isotonic sodium/chloride solution
classes.role_note: Common crystalloid for resuscitation/replacement and selected sodium/chloride needs; high chloride load can matter.

classes.name: Balanced isotonic crystalloids
classes.mechanism: Expand extracellular volume with electrolyte composition and metabolizable anions that reduce chloride burden versus saline
classes.role_note: Common resuscitation/replacement option; exact electrolyte composition differs by product.

classes.name: Dextrose-containing free-water solutions
classes.mechanism: Provide carbohydrate calories; after glucose metabolism the water distributes as electrolyte-free water
classes.target: Total-body water distribution after glucose uptake
classes.role_note: Used in selected maintenance/free-water contexts; not an initial volume-resuscitation fluid.

classes.name: Hypertonic sodium chloride
classes.mechanism: Raises extracellular sodium/osmolality and shifts water out of cells
classes.role_note: Emergency therapy for selected severe symptomatic hyponatremia; requires monitored correction targets.

classes.name: SIADH solute / osmotic water-excretion therapy
classes.mechanism: Increases solute excretion to facilitate electrolyte-free water clearance
classes.role_note: Second-line/context-dependent SIADH strategy after diagnosis and cause management.

classes.name: V2-receptor antagonist (aquaretic)
classes.mechanism: Blocks vasopressin V2 signaling, increasing electrolyte-free water excretion
classes.role_note: Selected euvolemic/hypervolemic hyponatremia under specialist guidance; not for emergency sodium correction.

classes.name: Desmopressin water-balance therapy
classes.mechanism: V2 agonism increases collecting-duct water reabsorption
classes.role_note: Central diabetes insipidus treatment; also used by specialists to control overcorrection in hyponatremia protocols.

classes.name: Oral potassium replacement
classes.mechanism: Replaces total-body potassium deficit
classes.role_note: Preferred route for many mild/moderate deficits when oral treatment is feasible.

classes.name: Intravenous potassium replacement
classes.mechanism: Directly replaces potassium when severe deficit, symptoms or inability to take oral therapy requires IV treatment
classes.role_note: High-alert medication; concentration/rate depend on access, severity and monitoring. Never IV push.

classes.name: Magnesium replacement
classes.mechanism: Restores magnesium required for membrane stability, ATP-dependent reactions and potassium/calcium homeostasis
classes.role_note: Oral or IV replacement depending on severity/symptoms and renal function.

classes.name: Calcium replacement / membrane stabilization
classes.mechanism: Raises ionized calcium and restores excitation-contraction/coagulation physiology
classes.role_note: Oral replacement for chronic deficiency; IV calcium for symptomatic hypocalcemia or selected hyperkalemia membrane stabilization.

classes.name: Phosphate replacement
classes.mechanism: Restores phosphate required for ATP, 2,3-DPG, membrane and skeletal physiology
classes.role_note: Oral or IV replacement based on severity, symptoms, refeeding risk and renal function.

classes.name: Bicarbonate / alkali therapy
classes.mechanism: Supplies bicarbonate to buffer hydrogen ions and raise serum bicarbonate/pH
classes.role_note: Selected severe metabolic acidosis, CKD metabolic acidosis and specific toxicologic/hyperkalemia contexts; treat the cause first.

classes.name: Human albumin solutions
classes.mechanism: Expands plasma oncotic pressure and intravascular volume; indication-specific albumin effects
classes.role_note: Specialized colloid for defined indications such as selected cirrhosis complications or plasma-volume contexts; not routine maintenance fluid.

classes.name: Thiamine for malnutrition/refeeding risk
classes.mechanism: Replenishes thiamine required for carbohydrate metabolism and pyruvate dehydrogenase activity
classes.role_note: Give before/with carbohydrate feeding in patients at meaningful deficiency/refeeding risk according to protocol.

classes.name: Multivitamin and trace-element replacement
classes.mechanism: Supplies essential vitamin cofactors and trace elements during inadequate intake or artificial nutrition
classes.role_note: Use deficiency- and nutrition-route-specific preparations; avoid indiscriminate megadosing.

classes.name: Oral nutrition supplements (ONS)
classes.mechanism: Increase energy/protein/micronutrient intake when diet alone is insufficient
classes.role_note: First-line nutrition support when the gut works and oral intake can be augmented.

classes.name: Standard polymeric enteral nutrition
classes.mechanism: Provides intact protein, carbohydrate, fat, water and micronutrients through the GI tract
classes.role_note: Preferred over PN when the GI tract is functional but oral intake is inadequate.

classes.name: Disease-specific / concentrated enteral nutrition
classes.mechanism: Adjusts energy density, protein, electrolyte or carbohydrate profile for selected clinical needs
classes.role_note: Use only when disease-specific composition offers a practical advantage; formula choice does not replace clinical targets.

classes.name: Parenteral amino-acid solutions
classes.mechanism: Provide intravenous amino acids for protein synthesis when enteral nutrition is not feasible/adequate
classes.role_note: Core macronutrient component of PN; g/kg target depends on illness, organ function and catabolic state.

classes.name: Parenteral dextrose
classes.mechanism: Provides intravenous carbohydrate calories
classes.role_note: Main carbohydrate macronutrient in PN; glucose infusion rate and total calories require individualized calculation.

classes.name: Intravenous lipid emulsions
classes.mechanism: Provide essential fatty acids and dense non-glucose calories
classes.role_note: PN macronutrient and essential-fatty-acid source; formulation-specific fatty-acid profile differs.

classes.name: Zinc replacement / diarrheal adjunct
classes.mechanism: Replenishes zinc needed for epithelial, immune and enzymatic functions
classes.role_note: Useful in documented deficiency and as WHO-recommended pediatric acute-diarrhea adjunct; adult routine use depends on indication.

labs.title: Women’s Health • Gynecology Pharmacology Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: WOMEN’S HEALTH • GYNECOLOGY • REPRODUCTIVE PHARMACOLOGY WORKSPACE
labs.subtitle: Clinical question → reproductive/gyne context → drug class → mechanism/target → formulation/route → learning dose → monitoring → source verification
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning CDS only. Contraception, abnormal uterine bleeding, PCOS, endometriosis, fertility treatment, menopause therapy and obstetric-emergency medicines require diagnosis, pregnancy status/intention, age, VTE/cardiovascular risk, migraine history, smoking, blood pressure, liver disease, cancer history, uterine pathology and concurrent medicines to be assessed. CDC MEC categories and current local/regulatory labeling must be checked before hormonal contraception. Fertility drugs and postpartum-haemorrhage medicines are specialist/emergency protocol therapies and are never auto-prescribed from a class card. No medicine is labelled “best” without a context-specific guideline recommendation.
classification_notes: Contraceptive efficacy, medical eligibility and patient preference are separate questions; a method can be highly effective yet medically inappropriate in a specific condition.
Heavy menstrual bleeding is a symptom, not a final diagnosis. Structural causes, pregnancy, anemia and bleeding disorders must be considered before simply suppressing bleeding.
PCOS treatment is goal-specific: cycle/endometrial protection, hyperandrogenism/metabolic risk and fertility are different therapeutic pathways.
Endometriosis pain suppression and infertility management are distinct; ovarian suppression does not itself improve fertility while actively suppressing ovulation.

Menopausal hormone therapy is individualized by symptoms, age/time since menopause, uterus status and thrombotic/cardiovascular/breast-cancer risk; local vaginal therapy is pharmacologically different from systemic therapy.
Ovulation induction, gonadotropins and PPH uterotonics require monitoring/protocol control; they are presented as specialist/emergency learning pathways, not routine OPD prescriptions.

classes.name: Combined hormonal contraceptives (estrogen + progestin)
classes.mechanism: Suppress ovulation through hypothalamic-pituitary feedback; progestin also thickens cervical mucus and alters endometrium
classes.role_note: Effective cycle control/contraception option when estrogen is medically eligible; requires CDC MEC-style risk screening.

classes.name: Progestin-only oral contraceptives
classes.mechanism: Primarily thicken cervical mucus; some formulations reliably suppress ovulation
classes.role_note: Estrogen-free oral contraception; timing rules and missed-pill instructions differ by formulation.

classes.name: Depot progestin injectable contraception
classes.mechanism: Sustained progestin suppresses ovulation, thickens cervical mucus and causes endometrial atrophy
classes.role_note: Long-acting injectable contraception; return to fertility and bone-density considerations differ from pills/implants.

classes.name: Progestin contraceptive implant
classes.mechanism: Continuous progestin suppresses ovulation and thickens cervical mucus
classes.role_note: Highly effective reversible contraception requiring insertion/removal procedure and interaction review.

classes.name: Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine systems
classes.mechanism: Local endometrial progestin causes endometrial suppression and thickens cervical mucus
classes.role_note: Long-acting contraception and major non-surgical option for heavy menstrual bleeding when anatomically suitable.

classes.name: Copper intrauterine device (non-hormonal contraceptive device)
classes.mechanism: Copper ions impair sperm function/fertilization; no systemic hormone
classes.role_note: Non-drug LARC and highly effective emergency-contraception option; may increase menstrual bleeding/cramping in some users.

classes.name: Emergency contraceptive pharmacotherapy
classes.mechanism: Delays or inhibits ovulation; does not terminate an established pregnancy
classes.target: Ovulation timing / progesterone receptor depending agent
classes.role_note: Time-sensitive pregnancy-prevention options after unprotected intercourse; method choice depends on timing, BMI/context, interactions and ongoing contraception plan.

classes.name: Antifibrinolytic therapy for heavy menstrual bleeding
classes.mechanism: Blocks plasminogen activation and reduces fibrin breakdown
classes.role_note: Non-hormonal episodic treatment option for HMB when thrombosis risk/contraindications are considered.

classes.name: NSAIDs for dysmenorrhea / HMB
classes.mechanism: COX inhibition reduces prostaglandin synthesis, decreasing uterine contractions and menstrual blood loss
classes.role_note: Useful for painful heavy periods in selected patients; not appropriate with renal/GI/bleeding contraindications.

classes.name: Oral progestins for AUB / cycle control
classes.mechanism: Progestational endometrial transformation and withdrawal stabilization
classes.role_note: Used for cyclic endometrial protection or bleeding control depending cause; regimen varies by indication.

classes.name: Insulin sensitizer in PCOS
classes.mechanism: Reduces hepatic glucose production and improves insulin sensitivity
classes.role_note: Metabolic/insulin-resistance therapy in appropriate PCOS patients; not a substitute for fertility-specific treatment when pregnancy is desired.

classes.name: Antiandrogen therapy for hirsutism/androgen symptoms
classes.mechanism: Reduces androgen receptor signaling or androgen conversion
classes.role_note: Adjunct for persistent hirsutism when reliable contraception is used; teratogenic fetal risk requires pregnancy prevention.

classes.name: Aromatase inhibitor for ovulation induction
classes.mechanism: Temporarily lowers estrogen synthesis, increasing endogenous FSH drive
classes.role_note: Guideline-preferred first-line pharmacologic ovulation induction for anovulatory infertility due to PCOS when no other infertility factor is present; off-label status varies by country.

classes.name: Selective estrogen receptor modulator for ovulation induction
classes.mechanism: Blocks hypothalamic estrogen feedback, increasing GnRH/FSH/LH release
classes.role_note: Alternative oral ovulation-induction agent; multiple-gestation and cycle-limit considerations require monitoring.

classes.name: Exogenous gonadotropins for ovulation induction / ovarian stimulation
classes.mechanism: Directly stimulate follicular development via FSH ± LH activity
classes.role_note: Specialist injectable fertility therapy requiring ultrasound/estradiol monitoring and OHSS/multiple-gestation prevention.

classes.name: Ovulation trigger agents
classes.mechanism: Mimic or induce LH surge to trigger final oocyte maturation/ovulation
classes.target: LH/hCG receptor or pituitary GnRH receptor
classes.role_note: Timing-critical fertility protocol component; choice affects OHSS risk and luteal support needs.

classes.name: GnRH antagonists for ART cycle control
classes.mechanism: Immediately block pituitary GnRH receptors to suppress premature LH surge
classes.role_note: ART stimulation-cycle control; not the same as oral GnRH antagonists used for endometriosis/fibroids.

classes.name: Progesterone luteal-phase support
classes.mechanism: Supports secretory endometrium and implantation through progesterone receptor activation
classes.role_note: Used in ART/luteal-support protocols; route and dose depend on protocol and product.

classes.name: Progestin therapy for endometriosis
classes.mechanism: Suppresses ovulation/endometrial proliferation and promotes decidualization/atrophy of ectopic endometrial tissue
classes.role_note: Common hormonal suppression strategy for endometriosis-associated pain when fertility is not being actively pursued.

classes.name: GnRH agonists for endometriosis
classes.mechanism: Initial stimulation followed by pituitary GnRH receptor downregulation and ovarian estrogen suppression
classes.role_note: Second-line/specialist ovarian-suppression therapy; hypoestrogenic effects often require duration limits/add-back planning.

classes.name: Oral GnRH antagonists for endometriosis/fibroid symptoms
classes.mechanism: Dose-dependently block pituitary GnRH receptors and reduce ovarian estrogen production
classes.role_note: Oral ovarian-suppression class; some products are combined with estradiol/progestin add-back and have duration/bone/liver restrictions.

classes.name: Systemic menopausal estrogen therapy
classes.mechanism: Replaces estrogen and stabilizes thermoregulatory/urogenital tissues
classes.role_note: Most effective pharmacologic therapy for vasomotor symptoms in appropriate patients; uterus status determines need for endometrial protection.

classes.name: Progestogen for endometrial protection with systemic estrogen
classes.mechanism: Opposes estrogen-driven endometrial proliferation
classes.role_note: Needed with systemic estrogen in most patients with an intact uterus unless an alternative adequate endometrial-protection strategy is used.

classes.name: Local genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) therapy
classes.mechanism: Restores local vaginal/urogenital estrogenic signaling or improves dyspareunia via local receptor modulation
classes.role_note: Local therapy for vaginal dryness/dyspareunia/urogenital symptoms; systemic exposure and risk profile differ by formulation.

classes.name: Nonhormonal pharmacotherapy for menopausal vasomotor symptoms
classes.mechanism: Modulates serotonergic/noradrenergic, GABAergic or neurokinin-B thermoregulatory pathways
classes.target: CNS thermoregulatory circuits / NK3 receptor depending agent
classes.role_note: Options when hormone therapy is unsuitable or not preferred; efficacy and adverse-effect profiles differ markedly.

classes.name: Pharmacotherapy for nausea/vomiting of pregnancy
classes.mechanism: Uses antihistaminic, vitamin-cofactor, dopamine or serotonin pathways to reduce nausea/vomiting
classes.role_note: Pregnancy-specific symptom treatment; dehydration, hyperemesis, electrolyte disturbance and alternate diagnoses must be assessed.

classes.name: Dopamine agonists for hyperprolactinemia
classes.mechanism: D2 receptor activation suppresses pituitary prolactin secretion
classes.role_note: Relevant to amenorrhea/galactorrhea/infertility when hyperprolactinemia is confirmed; requires cause evaluation.

classes.name: Uterotonics for postpartum haemorrhage prevention/treatment
classes.mechanism: Increase uterine smooth-muscle contraction through oxytocin, prostaglandin or adrenergic pathways
classes.role_note: Obstetric emergency medicines used within PPH protocols; contraindications differ by agent.

classes.name: Tranexamic acid in postpartum haemorrhage
classes.mechanism: Inhibits fibrinolysis by blocking plasminogen activation
classes.role_note: Time-sensitive adjunct in diagnosed PPH within a full emergency protocol; not a uterotonic and does not replace source control/resuscitation.

labs.title: Emergency • Crash-Cart • Antidote Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: EMERGENCY • RESUSCITATION • TOXICOLOGY • ANTIDOTE WORKSPACE
labs.subtitle: Emergency syndrome → immediate priorities → drug/antidote class → mechanism → protocol dose snapshot → monitoring → escalation/source verification
labs.scientific_boundary: High-risk clinician/research learning CDS only. This workspace does not replace ACLS/ALS, emergency department, ICU, poison-centre, toxicology, obstetric or institutional protocols. Resuscitation priorities (airway, breathing, circulation, CPR/defibrillation when indicated, decontamination/source control where appropriate, monitoring and rapid escalation) take precedence over drug browsing. Antidote selection depends on confirmed/suspected toxin, exposure timing/dose, ECG, acid-base/electrolytes, organ function and local availability. No automatic emergency prescription is generated.
classification_notes: Cardiac arrest drugs are adjuncts to high-quality CPR and defibrillation; calcium, bicarbonate and magnesium are not routine arrest drugs and belong only to selected circumstances.
Anaphylaxis is separated from routine allergy treatment: intramuscular epinephrine/adrenaline is the core first-line medicine; antihistamines and corticosteroids do not replace it.
Toxicology cards are syndrome/antidote maps, not self-treatment advice. Poison-centre/medical-toxicology support should be used early for serious, unknown or mixed exposures.
Anticoagulant reversal is indication- and agent-specific; reversal may carry thrombotic risk and should be coupled to bleeding severity, timing, renal function and procedural need.
Electrolyte rescue drugs (hypertonic saline, IV potassium/calcium/magnesium, insulin-dextrose) are high-alert medicines requiring monitored protocols.
Envenomation antivenom is indication-, geography-, species/syndrome- and product-specific; antivenom dosing is never inferred from a generic class card.

classes.name: Cardiac-arrest vasopressor
classes.mechanism: α/β adrenergic vasoconstriction and cardiac stimulation during resuscitation
classes.role_note: Adjunct to high-quality CPR/defibrillation according to ACLS; not a substitute for shock/CPR.

classes.name: Antiarrhythmics for shock-refractory VF/pVT
classes.mechanism: Suppress ventricular arrhythmia through multichannel or sodium-channel effects
classes.role_note: Amiodarone or lidocaine may be considered after defibrillation-resistant VF/pVT.

classes.name: Symptomatic bradycardia pharmacotherapy
classes.mechanism: Antimuscarinic and adrenergic chronotropic support
classes.role_note: Used only when bradycardia is producing cardiopulmonary compromise; pacing may be required.

classes.name: Regular narrow-complex tachycardia drug
classes.mechanism: Transient AV-nodal block
classes.role_note: For regular narrow-complex tachycardia after vagal maneuvers when appropriate.

classes.name: Stable wide-QRS tachycardia antiarrhythmic infusions
classes.mechanism: Suppress re-entry/ventricular arrhythmia via sodium or multichannel blockade
classes.role_note: For stable wide-complex tachycardia with expert consultation; unstable patients need synchronized cardioversion.

classes.name: Torsades / prolonged-QT polymorphic VT therapy
classes.mechanism: Magnesium stabilizes myocardial electrophysiology; remove QT-prolonging causes
classes.role_note: Use for torsades associated with prolonged QT; defibrillate immediately when unstable/pulseless.

classes.name: Anaphylaxis first-line adrenergic therapy
classes.mechanism: α1 vasoconstriction + β1 cardiac support + β2 bronchodilation/mast-cell mediator reduction
classes.role_note: IM epinephrine/adrenaline is the core first-line medicine; airway/oxygen/fluids/escalation are parallel priorities.

classes.name: Emergency bronchodilator adjuncts
classes.mechanism: β2 agonism ± antimuscarinic bronchodilation
classes.role_note: Adjunct for severe bronchospasm; does not replace epinephrine in anaphylaxis.

classes.name: Convulsive status epilepticus — benzodiazepine rescue
classes.mechanism: Enhances GABA-A inhibition
classes.role_note: Rapid first-line antiseizure rescue; airway/oxygen/glucose assessment occur simultaneously.

classes.name: Established status epilepticus — second-line antiseizure loading
classes.mechanism: Sodium-channel modulation or SV2A/GABA-related antiseizure activity
classes.role_note: Used after adequate benzodiazepine treatment if seizures persist; protocol/weight based.

classes.name: Severe hypoglycemia rescue
classes.mechanism: Provides glucose directly or mobilizes hepatic glycogen
classes.role_note: Rapid glucose restoration plus cause identification; recurrent hypoglycemia needs observation/infusion.

classes.name: Hyperkalemia — cardiac membrane stabilization
classes.mechanism: Raises myocardial threshold potential without lowering serum potassium
classes.role_note: IV calcium is for ECG toxicity/severe hyperkalemia contexts; it does not remove potassium.

classes.name: Hyperkalemia — intracellular potassium shift
classes.mechanism: Insulin stimulates Na/K ATPase; β2 agonism also shifts potassium intracellularly
classes.role_note: Temporizing potassium shift while definitive removal/cause treatment is arranged.

classes.name: Severe symptomatic hyponatremia rescue
classes.mechanism: Raises extracellular sodium/osmolality
classes.role_note: Hypertonic saline is protocol-controlled for severe neurologic symptoms; avoid overcorrection.

classes.name: Severe symptomatic hypocalcemia
classes.mechanism: Provides ionized calcium
classes.role_note: IV calcium for severe symptoms/ECG effects; correct magnesium and cause.

classes.name: Adrenal crisis emergency glucocorticoid
classes.mechanism: Replaces deficient glucocorticoid and supports vascular responsiveness
classes.role_note: Immediate steroid plus isotonic fluid/glucose/electrolyte management; do not delay for confirmatory testing.

classes.name: Opioid overdose reversal
classes.mechanism: Competitive opioid-receptor antagonism
classes.role_note: Restore ventilation and oxygenation; naloxone may require repeat dosing/infusion and does not replace airway/CPR.

classes.name: Selective benzodiazepine reversal
classes.mechanism: Competitive antagonism at benzodiazepine site on GABA-A receptor
classes.role_note: Flumazenil is a narrow-use antidote; it can precipitate seizures/withdrawal and is often inappropriate in mixed/unknown overdoses.

classes.name: Acetaminophen / paracetamol antidote
classes.mechanism: Replenishes glutathione and detoxifies reactive metabolite NAPQI
classes.role_note: N-acetylcysteine is time-sensitive; duration may be extended based on APAP level, liver tests and clinical course.

classes.name: Organophosphate/carbamate antidotal therapy
classes.mechanism: Atropine blocks muscarinic excess; oxime reactivates acetylcholinesterase in organophosphate poisoning
classes.role_note: Treat cholinergic toxidrome with airway/oxygen/suction/decontamination plus atropinization; oxime use depends on agent/timing/protocol.

classes.name: Toxic alcohol antidote
classes.mechanism: Inhibits alcohol dehydrogenase to prevent toxic metabolite formation
classes.role_note: Fomepizole is a core antidote for methanol/ethylene glycol poisoning; dialysis/folate or thiamine/pyridoxine adjuncts may also be required.

classes.name: Cyanide antidotes
classes.mechanism: Binds cyanide or enhances sulfur-dependent detoxification
classes.role_note: Severe suspected cyanide poisoning requires immediate supportive resuscitation plus antidote when indicated.

classes.name: Methemoglobinemia antidotal therapy
classes.mechanism: Accelerates reduction of methemoglobin to functional hemoglobin
classes.role_note: Treat significant symptomatic methemoglobinemia after removing oxidant exposure; G6PD status matters.

classes.name: Digoxin toxicity antidote
classes.mechanism: Binds free digoxin/digitalis glycosides
classes.role_note: Digoxin immune Fab for life-threatening digitalis toxicity; dose depends on known amount/level or empiric emergency protocol.

classes.name: Iron poisoning chelation
classes.mechanism: Chelates ferric iron to form ferrioxamine
classes.role_note: Deferoxamine is used for significant systemic iron toxicity; whole-bowel irrigation and supportive care may also be needed.

classes.name: TCA / sodium-channel blocker cardiotoxicity therapy
classes.mechanism: Sodium load and alkalinization counter fast sodium-channel blockade
classes.target: Cardiac fast sodium channels / serum pH
classes.role_note: Sodium bicarbonate is used when QRS widening, ventricular dysrhythmia, hypotension or severe sodium-channel toxicity is present; not routine for all poisonings.

classes.name: β-blocker poisoning rescue pharmacology
classes.mechanism: Supports cardiac output via cAMP-independent and metabolic/inotropic pathways
classes.role_note: Severe β-blocker poisoning may require glucagon, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy, vasopressors and advanced support under toxicology/ICU guidance.

classes.name: Calcium-channel blocker poisoning rescue pharmacology
classes.mechanism: Raises extracellular calcium and supports myocardial carbohydrate utilization/inotropy
classes.role_note: Severe CCB poisoning often requires IV calcium, high-dose insulin, vasopressors and advanced support.

classes.name: Local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST) rescue
classes.mechanism: Lipid emulsion acts as lipid sink/shuttle and metabolic support; modified resuscitation strategy is required
classes.role_note: ASRA checklist-driven emergency; airway/seizure management and lipid emulsion are core elements.

classes.name: Warfarin/VKA major-bleeding reversal
classes.mechanism: Replaces vitamin-K-dependent clotting factors and restores hepatic factor synthesis
classes.target: Factors II, VII, IX, X / vitamin K cycle
classes.role_note: Life-threatening bleeding commonly requires IV vitamin K plus 4-factor PCC per protocol; balance thrombosis risk.

classes.name: Dabigatran-specific reversal
classes.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody fragment binds dabigatran
classes.role_note: Idarucizumab is specific reversal for dabigatran in life-threatening/uncontrolled bleeding or urgent procedures.

classes.name: Factor-Xa inhibitor reversal
classes.mechanism: Decoy factor-Xa binding or nonspecific factor replacement
classes.role_note: Agent/timing/severity-specific reversal; andexanet availability and PCC alternatives vary by institution.

classes.name: Heparin reversal
classes.mechanism: Cationic protein complexes with unfractionated heparin; partially reverses LMWH
classes.role_note: Protamine dose depends on heparin type, amount and time since administration.

classes.name: Emergency antifibrinolytic support
classes.mechanism: Blocks plasminogen activation/fibrinolysis
classes.role_note: Tranexamic acid is context-specific (eg, trauma/PPH) and should follow indication-specific time windows/protocols.

classes.name: Malignant hyperthermia antidote
classes.mechanism: Reduces pathologic sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium release
classes.target: Ryanodine receptor (RyR1) / skeletal muscle calcium release
classes.role_note: Dantrolene plus immediate cessation of triggering agents, cooling and critical-care management.

classes.name: Serotonin syndrome pharmacologic adjuncts
classes.mechanism: Sedation reduces neuromuscular/autonomic activity; cyproheptadine antagonizes serotonin receptors
classes.role_note: Stop serotonergic agents and provide supportive cooling/fluids; benzodiazepines are core symptomatic therapy; cyproheptadine is an oral/NG adjunct.

classes.name: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome adjunct pharmacology
classes.mechanism: Dopamine agonism and/or skeletal-muscle calcium-release inhibition may reduce syndrome severity
classes.role_note: Stop dopamine antagonist, supportive ICU care, cooling/fluids; bromocriptine/dantrolene are specialist adjuncts, evidence is limited.

classes.name: Snake envenomation antivenom
classes.mechanism: Polyclonal antibodies neutralize circulating venom toxins
classes.role_note: Antivenom is indicated for clinical/systemic envenoming per regional protocol; product/species/geography and syndrome matter.

labs.title: Pediatrics • Child Health Pharmacology Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: PEDIATRIC PHARMACOLOGY • AGE/WEIGHT • FORMULATION • SAFETY WORKSPACE
labs.subtitle: Child/age band → clinical problem → drug class → pediatric formulation → age/weight dose discipline → monitoring → source verification
labs.scientific_boundary: Clinician/research learning CDS only. Pediatric prescribing is age-, weight-, indication-, formulation-, organ-function- and sometimes body-surface-area dependent. Neonates and critically ill children require separate institutional/neonatal/PALS protocols. The workspace never converts an adult dose into a child dose automatically and never treats a syrup concentration as a dose. Exact mg/kg, maximum dose, concentration, route, interval and duration must be verified before prescribing.
classification_notes: Use current measured weight in kilograms for weight-based dosing. Verify whether the source uses actual, ideal, adjusted or dosing weight for obesity/high-risk medicines.
Always separate dose (mg or mcg) from volume (mL). Liquid concentrations differ by product and country; calculate mL only after verifying the exact concentration.
Age cut-offs are drug- and indication-specific. Do not infer safety simply because a medicine appears in this lab.
Fever treatment is for distress/comfort, not just the number on the thermometer; red flags and serious-infection assessment take priority.
Acute diarrhea therapy prioritizes ORS and zinc in appropriate under-five contexts; antimicrobials are not routine for uncomplicated watery diarrhea.
Pediatric asthma management is age-stratified and inhaler/spacer technique is part of treatment. Controller and reliever strategies differ by age and severity.
Antibiotics are cross-linked as pediatric formulation/dose-learning classes, not automatic first-line choices; diagnosis, likely pathogen, allergy, resistance and local guideline must be checked.
Neonatal medicines, chemotherapy, sedation/anesthesia and intensive-care infusions are intentionally not generalized here.

classes.name: Pediatric non-opioid antipyretic/analgesic
classes.mechanism: Central prostaglandin modulation; analgesic and antipyretic effect
classes.role_note: For pain/distress with fever; fever red flags/serious illness assessment takes priority.

classes.name: Pediatric NSAID analgesic/antipyretic
classes.mechanism: COX inhibition reduces prostaglandin-mediated pain, fever and inflammation
classes.role_note: Alternative/adjunct analgesic-antipyretic in appropriately selected children.

classes.name: Pediatric short-acting β2 agonist (SABA)
classes.mechanism: β2-receptor agonism causes rapid bronchodilation
classes.role_note: Reliever bronchodilation; spacer/MDI technique is usually preferred when feasible.

classes.name: Pediatric short-acting antimuscarinic bronchodilator
classes.mechanism: Blocks muscarinic bronchoconstriction
classes.role_note: Adjunct in moderate-severe acute wheeze/asthma; not a routine standalone controller.

classes.name: Pediatric inhaled corticosteroids (ICS)
classes.mechanism: Local glucocorticoid anti-inflammatory activity reduces airway inflammation/exacerbation risk
classes.role_note: Foundational controller therapy in pediatric asthma; dose category is age/product/device specific.

classes.name: Pediatric ICS/LABA combination
classes.mechanism: ICS anti-inflammatory effect plus long-acting β2 bronchodilation
classes.role_note: Step-up controller; some formoterol-containing regimens may serve as MART/anti-inflammatory reliever depending on age/product/guideline.

classes.name: Leukotriene receptor antagonist
classes.mechanism: Blocks cysteinyl-leukotriene receptor signaling
classes.role_note: Alternative/add-on asthma/allergic-rhinitis therapy in selected children; generally less effective than ICS for asthma control.

classes.name: Second-generation H1 antihistamines
classes.mechanism: Peripheral H1-receptor blockade reduces histamine symptoms
classes.role_note: Preferred nonsedating/less-sedating oral allergy therapy in many pediatric contexts.

classes.name: Pediatric intranasal corticosteroids
classes.mechanism: Local nasal glucocorticoid anti-inflammatory activity
classes.role_note: High-value controller for persistent allergic rhinitis when age-approved.

classes.name: Pediatric anaphylaxis first-line epinephrine
classes.mechanism: α1 vasoconstriction + β1 cardiac support + β2 bronchodilation
classes.role_note: IM epinephrine is first-line; airway/oxygen/fluids/emergency escalation are parallel priorities.

classes.name: Pediatric oral rehydration therapy
classes.mechanism: Glucose-sodium cotransport promotes intestinal water/electrolyte absorption
classes.role_note: Foundation of acute watery-diarrhea dehydration management when oral rehydration is appropriate.

classes.name: Zinc for acute childhood diarrhea
classes.mechanism: Supports epithelial/immune function and reduces diarrhea duration/severity
classes.role_note: WHO adjunct to ORS in acute diarrhea in children under five.

classes.name: Selected pediatric antiemetic — 5-HT3 antagonist
classes.mechanism: Blocks serotonin 5-HT3 signaling in emetic pathways
classes.role_note: May facilitate oral rehydration in selected children with vomiting; not routine for every vomiting illness.

classes.name: Polyethylene glycol (macrogol) laxatives
classes.mechanism: Osmotic water retention softens stool
classes.role_note: First-line laxative family in pediatric constipation guidelines; disimpaction and maintenance regimens differ.

classes.name: Osmotic disaccharide laxative
classes.mechanism: Colonic fermentation increases osmotic water retention
classes.role_note: Alternative/add-on osmotic laxative depending age and protocol.

classes.name: Pediatric aminopenicillins
classes.mechanism: β-lactam inhibition of bacterial cell-wall synthesis
classes.role_note: Common pediatric antibacterial class; exact indication, dose intensity and duration are syndrome-specific.

classes.name: Aminopenicillin + β-lactamase inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Cell-wall inhibition plus β-lactamase inhibition
classes.role_note: Broader β-lactam option for selected infections when β-lactamase coverage is needed.

classes.name: Pediatric oral cephalosporins
classes.mechanism: β-lactam inhibition of cell-wall synthesis
classes.role_note: Selected alternatives/indication-specific therapy; spectrum differs greatly by generation/agent.

classes.name: Pediatric macrolides
classes.mechanism: Bind bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibit protein synthesis
classes.role_note: Used for selected atypical/pertussis/specific infections; not a generic substitute for β-lactams.

classes.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
classes.mechanism: Sequential folate-pathway inhibition
classes.role_note: Indication-specific antibacterial/anti-opportunistic therapy; age restrictions and contraindications matter.

classes.name: Pediatric parenteral third-generation cephalosporins
classes.mechanism: β-lactam cell-wall synthesis inhibition
classes.role_note: Hospital/protocol therapy for selected serious infections; meningitis/sepsis doses differ.

classes.name: Pediatric aminoglycosides — high alert
classes.mechanism: 30S ribosomal binding causes concentration-dependent bactericidal activity
classes.role_note: Serious Gram-negative/synergy contexts; dosing interval depends on age, renal function and protocol.

classes.name: Pediatric benzimidazole anthelmintics
classes.mechanism: Inhibit parasite microtubule function/glucose uptake
classes.role_note: Deworming/soil-transmitted helminth therapy in age- and epidemiology-appropriate contexts.

classes.name: Pediatric scabicides
classes.mechanism: Neurotoxic/paralytic effects on mites depending agent
classes.target: Mite sodium channels / glutamate-gated chloride channels
classes.role_note: Treat child and close contacts/environment per scabies protocol; age limits matter.

classes.name: Pediatric seizure rescue benzodiazepines
classes.mechanism: Enhance GABA-A inhibitory neurotransmission
classes.role_note: Time-critical rescue for prolonged convulsive seizure/status per pediatric emergency plan.

classes.name: Common pediatric maintenance antiseizure medicines
classes.mechanism: Reduce neuronal excitability via SV2A, sodium-channel or other antiseizure mechanisms
classes.role_note: Choice depends on seizure type/syndrome, age, comorbidity and reproductive safety.

classes.name: Pediatric oral iron / iron-deficiency therapy
classes.mechanism: Replenishes elemental iron for hemoglobin synthesis and iron stores
classes.role_note: Prevention/public-health supplementation and treatment of iron-deficiency anemia are different dosing pathways.

classes.name: Pediatric vitamin D preparations
classes.mechanism: Supports calcium/phosphate absorption and bone mineralization via vitamin-D receptor
classes.role_note: Prevention and deficiency/rickets treatment require different age- and diagnosis-specific regimens.

classes.name: Pediatric emollients / barrier therapy
classes.mechanism: Restores stratum-corneum hydration and barrier function
classes.role_note: Foundation of eczema care; regular liberal use reduces dryness/itch and steroid need.

classes.name: Pediatric topical corticosteroids — potency/site disciplined
classes.mechanism: Local glucocorticoid anti-inflammatory action
classes.role_note: Use the lowest effective potency for site/severity and limited duration; face/flexures/infants require extra caution.

classes.name: Topical calcineurin inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Inhibit calcineurin-dependent T-cell activation/cytokine transcription
classes.role_note: Steroid-sparing therapy for selected atopic-dermatitis sites/ages.

classes.name: Pediatric cough/cold medicine safety gate
classes.mechanism: Symptom-relief products have heterogeneous antihistamine/decongestant/antitussive mechanisms
classes.role_note: Safety/avoidance gate rather than a treatment class: young children should not receive adult-style multi-ingredient cough/cold products by default.

labs.subtitle: Symptom/diagnosis → anatomic site → drug class → local/systemic route → mechanism → formulation → monitoring → referral/safety gate
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning CDS only. Ear and eye symptoms can represent time-sensitive disease. Sudden hearing loss, mastoid/neurologic signs, severe orbital symptoms, painful red eye, photophobia, reduced vision, corneal opacity/ulcer, chemical injury, acute angle closure, ocular trauma and contact-lens-associated keratitis require urgent specialist/emergency assessment. Topical ocular steroids, intraocular-pressure lowering emergencies, intravitreal therapy and systemic therapy for sudden sensorineural hearing loss are not routine self-directed prescribing. Exact product concentration, tympanic-membrane status, ocular diagnosis, contact-lens status, age, pregnancy, organ function, interactions and current label/guideline must be verified.
classification_notes: ENT pharmacology is site-specific: external ear, middle ear, nose/sinus, pharynx/larynx and vestibular disorders should not be merged into one “ENT infection” pathway.
Acute otitis externa is primarily treated with topical therapy; non-ototoxic preparations are preferred when tympanic-membrane perforation or a tube is known/suspected.
Cerumen impaction treatment depends on symptoms, examination and modifying factors; cerumenolytics/irrigation/manual removal are options, not automatic prescriptions.
Acute sinusitis and sore throat are commonly viral; antimicrobial stewardship and diagnostic criteria should determine whether an antibiotic is indicated.
BPPV is fundamentally a repositioning-maneuver disorder. Vestibular suppressants may reduce short-term symptoms but should not replace canalith repositioning.
A sudden sensorineural hearing-loss presentation is an urgent time-sensitive ENT pathway, not a routine “ear-block” complaint.
Red eye must be triaged for pain, photophobia, visual loss, contact-lens use, corneal findings, trauma/chemical exposure and glaucoma before selecting drops.
Routine acute conjunctivitis is frequently viral or self-limited; topical antibiotics are not automatically indicated for every red eye.
Ocular corticosteroids can worsen infection and raise intraocular pressure; use requires a clear diagnosis and appropriate ophthalmic supervision.
Glaucoma treatment is IOP-target and disease-course based. Drug classes are learning options; patient-specific target pressure and ocular/systemic contraindications determine selection.
Intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy and acute angle-closure treatment are specialist/procedural pathways and are included for research understanding, not routine clinic drafting.

classes.name: Cerumenolytics / earwax-softening agents
classes.mechanism: Hydrate, emulsify or chemically soften impacted cerumen
classes.role_note: Option for symptomatic/obstructive cerumen when no contraindication to drops/irrigation; exam and modifying factors matter.

classes.name: Topical fluoroquinolones for acute otitis externa
classes.mechanism: Inhibit bacterial DNA gyrase/topoisomerase; high local concentration in ear canal
classes.role_note: Common topical antibacterial class for diffuse AOE; useful when non-ototoxic topical therapy is desired.

classes.name: Non-quinolone topical antibiotic / antibiotic-steroid ear drops
classes.mechanism: Local antibacterial activity ± glucocorticoid anti-inflammatory effect
classes.role_note: Alternative AOE preparations when tympanic membrane is intact and product-specific risks are acceptable.

classes.name: Acidifying / antiseptic otic agents
classes.mechanism: Lower ear-canal pH and create an environment less favorable to bacterial/fungal growth
classes.role_note: Selected mild AOE/prevention contexts; not for severe disease or uncertain TM status.

classes.name: Acute otitis media — systemic β-lactam class
classes.mechanism: Inhibit bacterial cell-wall synthesis
classes.role_note: Antibiotic class only when AOM diagnostic/severity criteria support antimicrobial therapy; observation is appropriate in selected patients.

classes.name: Intranasal corticosteroids
classes.mechanism: Local glucocorticoid receptor activation reduces nasal mucosal inflammation
classes.role_note: Core anti-inflammatory therapy for allergic rhinitis; also used in selected chronic/rhinosinusitis contexts.

classes.name: Intranasal H1 antihistamines
classes.mechanism: Local H1 receptor blockade reduces histamine-mediated nasal symptoms
classes.role_note: Rapid-onset rhinitis therapy; can combine with intranasal steroid in selected moderate-severe disease.

classes.name: Second-generation oral H1 antihistamines
classes.mechanism: Peripheral H1 receptor antagonism
classes.role_note: Useful particularly for sneezing/itch/rhinorrhea; generally less effective for congestion than intranasal steroids.

classes.name: Saline nasal therapy
classes.mechanism: Mechanical hydration, mucus thinning and allergen/debris clearance
classes.role_note: Low-risk adjunct for rhinitis and rhinosinusitis; irrigation water safety matters.

classes.name: Topical nasal α-adrenergic decongestants
classes.mechanism: Vasoconstrict nasal capacitance vessels to reduce edema
classes.role_note: Short-term congestion relief; prolonged use risks rhinitis medicamentosa.

classes.name: Systemic sympathomimetic decongestants
classes.mechanism: Adrenergic vasoconstriction reduces nasal mucosal edema
classes.role_note: Selected short-term use; less favored when cardiovascular or urinary risks are present.

classes.name: Acute bacterial rhinosinusitis — systemic antibiotic options
classes.mechanism: Pathogen-directed systemic antibacterial therapy
classes.role_note: Only for presentations meeting bacterial rhinosinusitis criteria/severity; many acute sinusitis cases do not need antibiotics.

classes.name: Acute sore-throat symptomatic analgesia
classes.mechanism: Analgesic/anti-inflammatory modulation reduces throat pain and fever
classes.role_note: Symptom relief while applying clinical scoring/red-flag assessment and antimicrobial stewardship.

classes.name: Streptococcal pharyngitis — narrow-spectrum penicillins
classes.mechanism: β-lactam inhibition of bacterial cell-wall synthesis
classes.role_note: Use only when clinical/testing strategy supports streptococcal infection; narrow-spectrum therapy is preferred when appropriate.

classes.name: Vestibular suppressants / antiemetics
classes.mechanism: Central H1/antimuscarinic or dopamine-antagonist effects reduce vestibular nausea/vertigo symptoms
classes.target: Vestibular nuclei / H1 / muscarinic / dopamine pathways
classes.role_note: Short-term symptom control only; BPPV treatment should prioritize canalith repositioning rather than routine suppressants.

classes.name: Ménière disease symptom-modifying agents
classes.mechanism: Varied proposed effects on inner-ear fluid dynamics/microcirculation
classes.role_note: Specialist-context pharmacology; evidence and availability vary by region.

classes.name: Topical vasoconstrictor / hemostatic adjuncts for epistaxis
classes.mechanism: Local vasoconstriction or antifibrinolysis supports hemostasis
classes.role_note: Adjunct to compression and definitive local management; recurrent/severe bleeding needs cause assessment.

classes.name: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss — corticosteroid pathway
classes.mechanism: Glucocorticoid anti-inflammatory/immunomodulatory effects
classes.role_note: Urgent ENT pathway; systemic or intratympanic corticosteroids are time-sensitive specialist decisions.

classes.name: Ocular lubricants / artificial tears
classes.mechanism: Replace or stabilize tear film and reduce ocular surface friction
classes.role_note: Foundational symptomatic dry-eye therapy; preservative burden matters with frequent use.

classes.name: Dry-eye immunomodulatory agents
classes.mechanism: Reduce ocular-surface T-cell/inflammatory signaling or neuro-inflammatory pathways
classes.role_note: Prescription therapy for selected chronic inflammatory dry eye after diagnosis and staged management.

classes.name: Topical dual-action antihistamine / mast-cell stabilizers
classes.mechanism: H1 antagonism plus mast-cell stabilization reduces itch and allergic inflammation
classes.role_note: Common first-line pharmacologic class for allergic conjunctivitis after allergen avoidance/cool compresses.

classes.name: Ocular mast-cell stabilizers
classes.mechanism: Stabilize mast cells and reduce mediator release
classes.role_note: Preventive/maintenance option; slower onset than dual-action agents.

classes.name: Topical antibiotics for bacterial conjunctivitis
classes.mechanism: Local antibacterial inhibition of bacterial growth/replication
classes.role_note: For suspected bacterial conjunctivitis when treatment is indicated; many red eyes are viral/allergic and do not benefit.

classes.name: Blepharitis topical antimicrobials
classes.mechanism: Reduce lid-margin bacterial load and inflammation
classes.role_note: Adjunct to lid hygiene/warm compresses in selected anterior/posterior blepharitis.

classes.name: Topical ophthalmic corticosteroids
classes.mechanism: Glucocorticoid receptor activation suppresses ocular inflammation
classes.role_note: Specialist-directed anti-inflammatory therapy only after excluding infection and clarifying diagnosis.

classes.name: Prostaglandin analogues / prostamides
classes.mechanism: Increase uveoscleral aqueous outflow
classes.role_note: Common first-line IOP-lowering class for open-angle glaucoma/ocular hypertension.

classes.name: Ophthalmic β-blockers
classes.mechanism: Reduce aqueous humor production via β-adrenergic blockade
classes.role_note: Effective IOP-lowering class but systemic cardiopulmonary contraindications matter.

classes.name: Ophthalmic α2-adrenergic agonists
classes.mechanism: Reduce aqueous production and increase uveoscleral outflow
classes.role_note: Adjunct/alternative IOP-lowering class.

classes.name: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (ocular/systemic)
classes.mechanism: Reduce bicarbonate-dependent aqueous humor secretion
classes.role_note: Topical chronic IOP lowering; systemic acetazolamide is also used in acute/high-IOP specialist contexts.

classes.name: Rho-kinase inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Increases trabecular outflow and may reduce episcleral venous pressure
classes.role_note: Newer topical IOP-lowering class, often adjunctive.

classes.name: Cholinergic miotics
classes.mechanism: Muscarinic activation contracts ciliary muscle and increases trabecular outflow
classes.role_note: Selected glaucoma/angle-closure use; less common for chronic POAG because of side effects.

classes.name: Hyperosmotic agents for acute severe IOP elevation
classes.mechanism: Increase plasma osmolality to draw water from vitreous and lower IOP
classes.role_note: Emergency ophthalmology pathway when indicated; systemic volume/renal/cardiac status matters.

classes.name: Mydriatics / cycloplegics
classes.mechanism: Block muscarinic receptors or stimulate α1 receptors to dilate pupil and/or paralyze accommodation
classes.role_note: Diagnostic/procedural ophthalmic class; angle-closure risk and age-specific use matter.

classes.name: Intravitreal anti-VEGF agents
classes.mechanism: Neutralize VEGF signaling to reduce vascular permeability/neovascularization
classes.role_note: Retina-specialist intravitreal therapy for neovascular AMD, diabetic macular edema and other retinal vascular indications.

classes.name: Ocular antiviral therapy
classes.mechanism: Inhibit herpesvirus DNA replication
classes.target: Viral DNA polymerase / thymidine-kinase dependent activation
classes.role_note: Herpetic ocular disease requires diagnosis because epithelial keratitis, stromal disease and uveitis use different antiviral/steroid strategies.

drugs.dose_example: Typical OTC learning snapshot: product-specific drops for short courses; verify label and intact tympanic membrane.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Do not use blindly with ear pain, drainage, tubes, perforation or recent ear surgery.

drugs.dose_example: Product-specific drops, commonly twice daily for ~7 days; verify exact combination/label.
drugs.role: Topical antibacterial ± anti-inflammatory treatment for AOE.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Do not substitute eye/ear formulations without checking product. Consider malignant OE red flags.

drugs.monitoring_pearl: Avoid when TM perforation/tube is suspected unless product is explicitly safe; neomycin can cause contact sensitization and aminoglycosides raise ototoxicity concern.

drugs.dose_example: Product-specific; verify exact formulation and indication.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Ototoxicity risk matters with non-intact TM; use only with clear indication and product guidance.

drugs.dose_example: Product-specific drops several times daily; verify label and TM status.

drugs.dose_example: Usually once daily; product/age specific.

labs.title: Endocrinology • Hormone • Metabolic Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: ADRENAL • PITUITARY • GONADAL • OBESITY • PARATHYROID
labs.subtitle: Specialist-oriented endocrine pharmacology: adrenal replacement/crisis, cortisol excess, primary aldosteronism, prolactinoma, acromegaly, hypopituitarism, AVP deficiency, male hypogonadism/fertility, obesity pharmacotherapy and parathyroid disorders.
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning CDS only. Endocrine therapy is diagnosis-dependent and often requires biochemical confirmation, imaging, specialist follow-up and dynamic monitoring. Adrenal crisis must be treated emergently; catecholamine-secreting tumors require sequencing safeguards; testosterone is not for nonspecific age-related enhancement and suppresses fertility; obesity medicines must follow current product eligibility/contraindications; pituitary/adrenal tumor drugs and PTH replacement are specialist-controlled. Exact product, formulation, dose, titration, organ function, pregnancy/reproductive plans, interactions and current label/guideline must be verified.
classification_notes: Diabetes and thyroid pharmacology remain in their dedicated existing labs; this module fills the major remaining endocrine gaps.
Adrenal replacement is separated from cortisol-lowering therapy to avoid indication confusion.
Pituitary hormone excess (prolactinoma/acromegaly/Cushing disease) is separated from hormone-deficiency replacement.
Weight-management medicines are chronic-disease therapies, not cosmetic or automatic prescriptions.
Endocrine emergencies and tumor-directed therapies are protocol/specialist controlled.

classes.name: Physiologic glucocorticoid replacement
classes.mechanism: Replaces deficient cortisol activity
classes.role_note: Core chronic replacement in confirmed adrenal insufficiency; sick-day education and emergency planning are essential.

classes.name: Mineralocorticoid replacement
classes.mechanism: Replaces aldosterone effect
classes.role_note: For primary adrenal insufficiency with mineralocorticoid deficiency.

classes.name: Adrenal-crisis emergency glucocorticoid
classes.mechanism: Rapidly restores glucocorticoid activity
classes.role_note: Emergency treatment must not wait for confirmatory testing when adrenal crisis is strongly suspected.

classes.name: Glucocorticoid withdrawal / HPA-axis recovery support
classes.mechanism: Gradual dose reduction permits HPA-axis recovery after chronic exogenous glucocorticoid exposure
classes.role_note: Not a fixed drug regimen; taper depends on underlying disease, exposure, symptoms and testing context.

classes.name: Cortisol synthesis inhibitors — azole related
classes.mechanism: Inhibits adrenal steroidogenic enzymes
classes.role_note: Specialist medical therapy when surgery is not curative/possible or as bridge.

classes.name: Cortisol synthesis inhibitors — non-azole
classes.mechanism: Inhibits adrenal cortisol-synthesis enzymes
classes.role_note: Specialist cortisol-lowering therapy.

classes.name: Pituitary-directed therapy for Cushing disease
classes.mechanism: Reduces ACTH secretion from corticotroph tumor
classes.role_note: Specialist pituitary-directed therapy; not a substitute for etiologic evaluation.

classes.name: Glucocorticoid-receptor antagonism
classes.mechanism: Blocks cortisol action rather than lowering cortisol concentration
classes.role_note: Selected endogenous Cushing syndrome with hyperglycemia; specialist monitoring.

classes.name: Adrenolytic therapy
classes.mechanism: Adrenocortical cytotoxic/adrenolytic action
classes.role_note: Specialist therapy particularly in adrenocortical carcinoma contexts.

classes.name: Primary aldosteronism — mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists
classes.mechanism: Blocks aldosterone effect
classes.role_note: Medical therapy for bilateral disease or when surgery is not chosen/appropriate.

classes.name: Primary aldosteronism — ENaC blockade
classes.mechanism: Blocks epithelial sodium channel downstream of aldosterone
classes.role_note: Alternative when MRA is not tolerated/appropriate.

classes.name: Pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma — alpha blockade
classes.mechanism: Blocks catecholamine-mediated alpha-adrenergic vasoconstriction
classes.role_note: Preoperative/symptom control under specialist supervision; beta-blockade must never precede adequate alpha blockade in catecholamine-secreting disease.

classes.name: Catecholamine synthesis inhibition
classes.mechanism: Inhibits tyrosine hydroxylase
classes.role_note: Adjunct for severe catecholamine excess or selected metastatic/inoperable disease.

classes.name: Dopamine agonists for prolactinoma
classes.mechanism: D2 receptor agonism suppresses prolactin secretion and often shrinks tumor
classes.role_note: First-line pharmacologic pathway for most symptomatic prolactinomas after cause evaluation.

classes.name: Acromegaly — first-generation somatostatin receptor ligands
classes.mechanism: Suppresses GH secretion via somatostatin receptors
classes.role_note: Medical therapy when surgery is not curative/appropriate and in selected primary medical therapy settings.

classes.name: Acromegaly — broader somatostatin receptor ligand
classes.mechanism: Suppresses GH through broader SSTR binding
classes.role_note: Specialist option in selected inadequately controlled disease.

classes.name: Growth-hormone receptor antagonist
classes.mechanism: Blocks peripheral GH receptor signaling and lowers IGF-1
classes.role_note: Specialist option when biochemical control is inadequate.

classes.name: Acromegaly — dopamine agonist adjunct
classes.mechanism: D2 agonism may reduce GH secretion in selected tumors
classes.role_note: Oral adjunct in mild disease or combination therapy; specialist selected.

classes.name: Growth-hormone replacement
classes.mechanism: Replaces deficient GH signaling
classes.role_note: For rigorously confirmed GH deficiency; specialist titration.

classes.name: Arginine vasopressin deficiency (central DI) replacement
classes.mechanism: V2 receptor agonism increases renal water reabsorption
classes.role_note: Desmopressin replacement for confirmed central AVP deficiency; avoid over-replacement.

classes.name: Testosterone replacement for confirmed male hypogonadism
classes.mechanism: Restores androgen action
classes.role_note: Only for men with compatible symptoms/signs plus consistently low testosterone after etiologic evaluation; not for age-related enhancement.

classes.name: Gonadotropins for hypogonadotropic male infertility
classes.mechanism: LH/hCG and FSH activity stimulates intratesticular testosterone and spermatogenesis
classes.role_note: Specialist fertility-directed treatment; testosterone replacement is inappropriate when fertility is the goal.

classes.name: Obesity pharmacotherapy — GLP-1 receptor agonists
classes.mechanism: Enhances satiety and slows gastric emptying through GLP-1 signaling
classes.role_note: Chronic weight-management pharmacotherapy only when label criteria and contraindications are met; lifestyle support remains foundational.

classes.name: Obesity pharmacotherapy — dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist
classes.mechanism: Dual incretin receptor agonism increases satiety and supports weight reduction
classes.role_note: Chronic weight-management therapy for indicated patients.

classes.name: Obesity pharmacotherapy — intestinal lipase inhibition
classes.mechanism: Reduces absorption of dietary fat
classes.role_note: Non-incretin weight-management option.

classes.name: Obesity pharmacotherapy — phentermine/topiramate ER
classes.mechanism: Sympathomimetic appetite suppression plus topiramate-related satiety effects
classes.role_note: Selected chronic weight-management option with reproductive/cardiovascular safeguards.

classes.name: Obesity pharmacotherapy — naltrexone/bupropion ER
classes.mechanism: Modulates hypothalamic appetite and reward pathways
classes.role_note: Selected chronic weight-management option.

classes.name: Obesity pharmacotherapy — short-term sympathomimetic
classes.mechanism: Increases norepinephrine signaling and suppresses appetite
classes.role_note: Short-term product-label context only; not suitable for many cardiovascular-risk patients.

classes.name: Genetic obesity — MC4 receptor agonism
classes.mechanism: Activates melanocortin-4 receptor signaling
classes.role_note: Only for specific genetically confirmed obesity syndromes under specialist care.

classes.name: Chronic hypoparathyroidism — conventional replacement
classes.mechanism: Replaces calcium and active vitamin-D effect
classes.role_note: Conventional therapy aims for symptom control while avoiding hypercalciuria/hypercalcemia.

classes.name: Chronic hypoparathyroidism — PTH replacement
classes.mechanism: Restores parathyroid-hormone signaling
classes.role_note: Specialist PTH-replacement option for selected adults not adequately controlled with conventional therapy.

classes.name: Hyperparathyroidism — calcimimetic
classes.mechanism: Activates calcium-sensing receptor to reduce PTH secretion
classes.role_note: Selected primary/secondary hyperparathyroid contexts; etiology and surgery candidacy remain central.

classes.name: Central precocious puberty — long-acting GnRH agonists
classes.mechanism: Continuous GnRH-receptor stimulation suppresses pituitary gonadotropin secretion
classes.role_note: Pediatric endocrinology specialist therapy after confirmation of central precocious puberty.

labs.title: Oncology • Cancer Pharmacology • Supportive Care Intelligence Lab
labs.eyebrow: CYTOTOXIC • TARGETED • IMMUNOTHERAPY • ENDOCRINE ONCOLOGY • SUPPORTIVE CARE
labs.subtitle: Research-oriented cancer pharmacology workspace: classic cytotoxic classes, biomarker-driven targeted therapy, immune checkpoint/cellular therapy, hormone-sensitive cancer therapy and essential oncology supportive-care pharmacology.
labs.scientific_boundary: Research/learning CDS only — not a chemotherapy order-set or dose calculator. Anticancer treatment is cancer-type, stage, histology, biomarker, prior-therapy, performance-status, body-size, organ-function and protocol dependent. Many agents are hazardous, vesicant, teratogenic, immunosuppressive or associated with fatal organ toxicities. Regimen construction, exact dose, cycle timing, premedication, dose modification, infusion handling, extravasation response, cellular therapy and immune-toxicity management require current oncology protocol, product label and specialist supervision. FDA accelerated-approval status and withdrawals can change; verify current regulatory status before use.
classification_notes: This module classifies pharmacology by mechanism and supportive-care function; it does not recommend a cancer regimen automatically.
Targeted therapy and immunotherapy require tumor-, stage- and biomarker-specific selection; the same drug can have very different indications across cancers.
Classic cytotoxic drugs are separated from targeted therapy, immune therapy and endocrine oncology to reduce category confusion.

Supportive-care lenses cover CINV, neutropenia prevention, bone complications, tumor lysis, immune-related toxicity and extravasation; antibiotic treatment of febrile neutropenia remains linked to the Antibiotic Lab.

Current approval/withdrawal status must be checked against FDA/other relevant regulator and local oncology protocol; older NCG documents are an India-context reference, not a substitute for current institutional guidance.

classes.name: Alkylating / DNA-damaging agents
classes.mechanism: Covalent DNA injury/cross-linking or related DNA damage
classes.role_note: Cytotoxic backbone used in multiple solid and hematologic malignancies; regimen-specific specialist use.

classes.name: Platinum compounds
classes.mechanism: DNA cross-linking and replication inhibition
classes.role_note: Core cytotoxic class with agent-specific renal, neurologic, auditory and marrow toxicities.

classes.name: Antimetabolites — pyrimidine-related
classes.mechanism: Disrupts nucleotide synthesis or DNA/RNA incorporation
classes.role_note: Widely used antimetabolite class; pharmacogenomic and organ-function issues can be critical.

classes.name: Antimetabolites — folate/purine pathways
classes.mechanism: Inhibits folate or purine metabolism / nucleotide synthesis
classes.role_note: Mechanistically diverse antimetabolites used in solid and hematologic cancer protocols.

classes.name: Anthracyclines
classes.mechanism: Topoisomerase-II inhibition, DNA intercalation and free-radical injury
classes.role_note: Highly effective cytotoxic class with cumulative cardiotoxicity and extravasation risk.

classes.name: Topoisomerase inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Inhibits topoisomerase I or II causing lethal DNA breaks
classes.role_note: Solid and hematologic cancer cytotoxics with agent-specific GI and marrow toxicity.

classes.name: Taxanes
classes.mechanism: Stabilizes microtubules and blocks mitosis
classes.role_note: Common solid-tumor cytotoxics with neuropathy, marrow and hypersensitivity risks.

classes.name: Vinca alkaloids
classes.mechanism: Inhibits microtubule polymerization
classes.role_note: Mitotic inhibitors; vinca agents have major neurotoxicity and route-safety concerns.

classes.name: Other microtubule inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Disrupts microtubule dynamics
classes.role_note: Later-line specialist cytotoxic options.

classes.name: Other classic cytotoxics
classes.mechanism: Agent-specific DNA injury or antitumor antibiotic effects
classes.role_note: Selected classic cytotoxic agents that do not fit the main mechanistic buckets.

classes.name: HER2-directed therapy
classes.mechanism: Blocks HER2 signaling or delivers HER2-directed therapy
classes.role_note: Biomarker-selected HER2-positive disease therapy; cardiac and pulmonary toxicities vary by agent.

classes.name: EGFR-directed therapy
classes.mechanism: Inhibits EGFR signaling
classes.role_note: Molecular selection matters; rash, diarrhea and interstitial lung disease are important class/agent risks.

classes.name: ALK / ROS1 kinase inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Inhibits oncogenic ALK/ROS1 signaling
classes.role_note: Driver-mutation selected NSCLC therapy; CNS activity and toxicity differ by agent.

classes.name: BCR-ABL tyrosine-kinase inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Suppresses BCR-ABL oncogenic kinase signaling
classes.role_note: Core precision therapy in Philadelphia chromosome/BCR-ABL disease; agent-specific vascular and pleuropulmonary risks.

classes.name: VEGF / VEGFR pathway inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Inhibits tumor angiogenesis signaling
classes.role_note: Antiangiogenic therapy across several cancers; hypertension, thrombosis/bleeding, wound healing and proteinuria are key issues.

classes.name: BRAF / MEK pathway inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Blocks MAPK signaling downstream of oncogenic BRAF
classes.role_note: Usually biomarker-selected and often combination based to delay resistance.

classes.name: CDK4/6 inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Blocks cyclin-dependent kinases 4/6 and cell-cycle progression
classes.role_note: Major HR-positive breast-cancer targeted class combined with endocrine therapy.

classes.name: PARP inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Exploits homologous-recombination repair defects / synthetic lethality
classes.role_note: Biomarker/indication-dependent maintenance or treatment; marrow toxicity and MDS/AML signal require surveillance.

classes.name: PI3K / AKT / mTOR pathway inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Inhibits oncogenic PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling
classes.role_note: Biomarker- and indication-specific targeted agents with metabolic and immune/toxicologic risks.

classes.name: Antibody-drug conjugates
classes.mechanism: Targeted antibody delivers cytotoxic payload to antigen-expressing tumor cells
classes.role_note: Rapidly evolving specialist class; indication and biomarker must match current approval/protocol.

classes.name: PD-1 / PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Releases inhibitory immune checkpoints to restore antitumor T-cell activity
classes.role_note: Tumor/biomarker- and stage-specific immunotherapy; immune-related adverse events can affect any organ.

classes.name: CTLA-4 / LAG-3 checkpoint therapy
classes.mechanism: Enhances T-cell activation through additional immune checkpoints
classes.role_note: Specialist immunotherapy often used in combination; immune toxicity burden can be substantial.

classes.name: Cellular therapy / bispecific T-cell engagers
classes.mechanism: Redirects or engineers immune cells to attack malignant cells
classes.role_note: Highly specialized hematologic-oncology therapy requiring certified centers/protocols and intensive toxicity monitoring.

classes.name: Breast-cancer endocrine therapy — SERM/SERD
classes.mechanism: Blocks or degrades estrogen-receptor signaling
classes.role_note: HR-positive breast-cancer endocrine therapy selected by stage, menopausal status, prior therapy and molecular context.

classes.name: Aromatase inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Suppresses peripheral estrogen synthesis
classes.role_note: Postmenopausal or ovarian-suppression-associated HR-positive breast-cancer therapy.

classes.name: GnRH agonist / antagonist cancer therapy
classes.mechanism: Suppresses gonadal sex-steroid production
classes.role_note: Used for ovarian suppression or androgen deprivation depending indication; flare and cardiovascular/metabolic issues vary by agent.

classes.name: Androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Blocks androgen receptor signaling
classes.role_note: Prostate-cancer systemic therapy combined/sequenced with ADT depending disease state.

classes.name: Androgen-synthesis inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Suppresses extragonadal/tumor androgen synthesis
classes.role_note: CYP17 inhibition in prostate cancer, generally with glucocorticoid support per protocol.

classes.name: CINV prevention — 5-HT3 antagonists
classes.mechanism: Blocks serotonin 5-HT3 signaling
classes.role_note: Antiemetic backbone chosen according to emetogenic risk and regimen.

classes.name: CINV prevention — NK1 antagonists
classes.mechanism: Blocks substance-P NK1 signaling
classes.role_note: Used as part of multidrug prophylaxis for higher emetogenic risk.

classes.name: CINV multimodal adjuncts
classes.mechanism: Multiple antiemetic mechanisms
classes.role_note: Adjuncts combined according to chemotherapy emetogenicity, prior control and patient risk.

classes.name: Myeloid growth factors (G-CSF)
classes.mechanism: Stimulates neutrophil production and maturation
classes.role_note: Primary/secondary febrile-neutropenia prophylaxis depends on regimen risk and patient factors; not a substitute for urgent fever assessment.

classes.name: Bone-modifying therapy in cancer
classes.mechanism: Inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption
classes.role_note: Prevents skeletal-related events in selected bone metastasis/myeloma contexts; dental and renal/calcium safety are essential.

classes.name: Tumor-lysis syndrome prophylaxis / treatment
classes.mechanism: Reduces uric acid formation or rapidly degrades uric acid
classes.role_note: Risk-stratified TLS prevention/treatment requires hydration, frequent chemistry monitoring and disease-specific protocol.

classes.name: Immune-related adverse-event immunosuppression
classes.mechanism: Suppresses immune-mediated organ inflammation caused by checkpoint therapy
classes.role_note: Organ- and grade-specific toxicity management; specialist protocols determine when to hold immunotherapy and which immunosuppressant to use.

classes.name: Chemotherapy extravasation antidotes
classes.mechanism: Agent-specific neutralization or tissue dispersion after vesicant extravasation
classes.role_note: Extravasation is a time-critical protocol event; stop infusion, preserve line as appropriate and follow agent-specific institutional pathway.
